title: Forced-L2 stress run fails with fresh caches: save-all off-ramp merge, reachable impossible code
description:
With the optimizer forced (OptimizationLevel SIMPLE_TRANSLATION and FIRST_JVM_TRANSLATION countdowns at 10, L2Optimizer.shouldSanityCheck and L2ValueManifest.deepManifestDebugCheck on) and fresh module caches, `./gradlew test --tests avail.test.AvailTest` fails 7 of 24 at HEAD 5b92b20bc (verified in a clean worktree, 2026-11-20).  Two distinct failures; the rest are OverlappingFileLockException fallout:

1. "List has more than one element" in JVMTranslator.saveAllFeeding: an L2_CREATE_CONTINUATION ("Create a reification continuation", from L1Translator's reification path) sits in an "Off-ramp" block with two predecessors: the L2_SAVE_ALL_AND_PC_TO_INT ("Forced split #1339") fall-through and an edge-split jump.  saveAllFeeding assumes the create is reached only from its save-all's fall-through.  Seen while optimizing the date-explosion function (timestamp → exploded fields) during library compilation.
2. L2_IMPOSSIBLE_CODE reached at run time in a JVM chunk for the Phrases.avail semantic restriction of "`«<«_‡,»>`»" (block #1), called from From_to_do_, while loading Examples / Convenient ASCII.

Earlier forced runs passed only because valid module caches skipped compiling most modules, so far less code ran under forced optimization.  The repository version bump in avail-iel.5 (V20) forces full recompilation, which is how this surfaced.

title: Split label types from a single continuation primitive type, and switch the library
description:
Split the types: ContinuationTypeDescriptor becomes LabelTypeDescriptor (the $[…]→R types), and continuations get a single primitive type, PrimitiveTypeDescriptor.Types.CONTINUATION(), named "continuation" in Avail.  The most general label type is the special object "label" (with "label meta" if warranted); "continuation meta" is retired.

- Type tags, special objects, serializer operations (bump the repository version), and every primitive's signature follow the split: continuation accessors, P_CreateContinuation, P_ResumeContinuation, and P_GetContinuationOfOtherFiber use CONTINUATION(); restart, exit, and the type conversions use label types.
- The library and tests switch every label-typed use of "continuation" to "label", renaming any conflicting locals rather than the type.  generateAllNames, coverage modules for new primitives.

title: LabelDescriptor: labels as (caller, function) objects
description:
Introduce LabelDescriptor and A_Label: a label is (caller continuation, function), with no arguments, pc, stack, locals, or L2 state.  In this step a label's kind is still the existing continuation type for its function type, so type checks are unchanged.

- Label creation (L1 stepper, L2Simple_PushLabel, L2_VIRTUAL_CREATE_LABEL's replacement) builds a Label.  L2_VIRTUAL_CREATE_LABEL's replacement reduces to reifying the caller (when needed) and building the Label: no save-all, register dump, or L2 entry point.
- Restart restores the label's caller and calls its function with the supplied arguments, entering the function normally (so the interrupt check on entry runs).  L2's recognition of a restart of the frame's own label as a loop (back edge to the restart loop head) is kept.
- Exit returns the value to the label's caller.
- Accessors: A_Label caller/function; primitives to read a label's caller and function.
- Serialization of labels; the debugger presents labels as values.

title: Remove restarting a label with its original arguments
description:
Remove restarting a label with its original (implicit) arguments, so that a label never needs to capture its frame's arguments.

- Remove the Restart_ primitive (P_RestartContinuation) and the L2_RESTART_CONTINUATION operation, which only it used, along with its binding, names, exports, and coverage test module.
- Rewrite every plain "Restart x" in the library, its tests, and the examples as "Restart x with <...>", passing the label's function's own parameters.  The generator's execution state needed a real change: its start block now takes one ignored argument, so both kinds of execution-state label take one argument and can be restarted the same way.
- AvailPushLabel.fixUsageFlags no longer keeps arguments alive for a later push-label.
- Every place that creates a label (the L1 stepper, L2Simple_PushLabel, L2_VIRTUAL_CREATE_LABEL through createLabelContinuation or L2_CREATE_CONTINUATION) fills the argument slots with nil instead of reading the arguments; L2_VIRTUAL_CREATE_LABEL lost its arguments operand.
- Regenerate the bootstrap names, and prune the stranded keys the regeneration left at the tail of PrimitiveNames_en.properties, including a "*=" fragment left by a broken hand edit in 71ed5630b and a truncated P_TupleAppend comment.

Also check that P_CreateContinuation (the synthetic base frame in Exceptions.avail) still works with only dynamic checks.

title: Create labels with a primitive instead of the L1 push-label nybblecode
description:
Replace the L1 nybblecode L1Ext_doPushLabel with a special, real primitive that creates a label, shrinking the nybblecode set.  It currently has 16 basic operations plus 7 extended ones.

Mark's sketch: the primitive takes a function and a tuple of arguments, forces a reification if the tracked call depth is greater than 1, and uses the grand-caller (one or two levels down, depending on the tracked call depth) as the label's caller.
design:
Points to think through (from the 2026-11-20 discussion):
- Which caller.  The label belongs to the function F that invokes the primitive, so its caller is F's caller.  After reification the top continuation is F, stopped at the primitive's call site, and the label's caller is that continuation's caller.  Whether that is one or two levels down depends on whether invoking the primitive pushed a frame of its own, which is what the tracked call depth tells.  Work out exactly when reification is needed: if F is already reified, or the call is in a reification handler, none is needed.
- Where the function and arguments come from.  L1 has no operation that pushes the current function, and a function with outers cannot be a literal.  Two options: (a) the compiler finds a way to push F and its arguments (L1_doMakeTuple over the argument slots handles the tuple); or (b) the primitive reads them from F's reified continuation and takes no arguments.  Mark's sketch passes them explicitly, which also lets a label name any function and arguments; the primitive must then check the arguments against the function's parameter types.
- Unification with the optimizer.  avail-bjv models a label in L2 as CreateLabel(caller, function, CreateTuple(arguments)).  If the real primitive takes (function, arguments) and supplies the caller itself, the L2 invocation and the primitive are the same operation, and the L1Translator needs no special case for labels beyond the primitive's own L2 generation.
- Removing the nybblecode touches the L1 instruction set (L1Operation, L1InstructionWriter, decoder and disassembler, L1Decompiler, the L1 interpreter, L1Translator, the compiler's label emission), so compiled modules change: bump the repository version.
- Depends on the LabelDescriptor existing, if the primitive answers a Label.
notes:
Mark, 2026-11-20:
- Passing the arguments explicitly removes the push-label-specific hacks that force the arguments to stay alive.
- The primitive could be a bootstrap primitive named by a pragma in Origin.avail.
- Block syntax would need reworking so that a label can occur anywhere in a function, but still only to restart or exit that function.

Corrected caller accounting (supersedes the design's "Which caller" bullet): if the primitive is being invoked, the calling frame has definitely not been reified, whether it runs in L1, L2Simple, or L2.  What matters is whether that frame's own caller has been reified yet, since that continuation fills the label's caller field once it becomes immutable.  If the primitive has to reify, the caller of the primitive will definitely be reified, and then the grand-caller is the continuation the label captures.
2026-11-20 (5b92b20bc, ruling on avail-iel): a label captures no arguments, so the label-creation primitive needs no tuple of arguments.  It takes at most the function (or reads it from the reified frame), and supplies the caller itself.  The design's "Where the function and arguments come from" and "Unification" bullets are superseded on the arguments: the matching L2 invocation is CreateLabel(caller, function).
Ruling (Mark, 2026-11-20): rejected.  Label creation stays part of the block syntax and keeps its own nybblecode (L1Ext_doPushLabel); it does not become a real primitive, and the block syntax is not reworked to allow a label anywhere in a function.  The caller accounting worked out above still describes what label creation must do at run time: if the creating frame's caller is not yet reified, reify, and then the creating frame's caller is the label's caller.
close_reason: Rejected: label creation stays block syntax with its own nybblecode

title: Separate labels from continuations (LabelDescriptor, label types, CONTINUATION primitive type)
description:
Separate labels from continuations, as two independent kinds of value with independent types.

A label is (caller continuation, function): what L1_doPushLabel captures.  It has no arguments, pc, stack, locals, or L2 state.  Restarting a label restores its caller into the interpreter and calls its function with the arguments supplied to the restart (Restart_with_, the only form since avail-iel.3); exiting a label returns a value to its caller.  Labels compare structurally by those two parts.  A label *type* still describes the function's parameter types and return type, since a restart's arguments and an exit's value are checked against them.

A continuation represents only an activated execution frame, normally created as a side effect of calling a method (and by reification).  Its pc, stack, and locals are meaningful.

Today both are ContinuationDescriptor instances, told apart only by pc == 0, and the restart primitives (P_RestartContinuationWithArguments, P_RestartContinuationWithArgumentsIf) merely assert it; a continuation from P_ContinuationCaller has a type that admits it.  The split makes that distinction static.
design:
Rulings (Mark, 2026-11-20):
- The two type hierarchies are independent, at least until something shows otherwise.
- Repurpose ContinuationTypeDescriptor as LabelTypeDescriptor.  The syntax $[…]→R now means a label type.  The structure is unchanged: the argument types and the return type are both contravariant, and the most general label type has a bottom arguments tuple type ("…") and a bottom return type, so there is no separate lattice root.
- Continuations lose all type structure and become a single primitive type, PrimitiveTypeDescriptor.Types.CONTINUATION(), like CHARACTER() or MODULE(), spelled "continuation" in Avail.  Finding a continuation on the stack tells nothing useful statically about its argument or return types, so no $$ syntax is needed.
- Restart: restore the label's caller into the interpreter, then call the label's function with its arguments.  The label never becomes the running frame.  Exit: return the value to the label's caller.

Reach (survey, 2026-11-20):
- About 31 Kotlin files mention ContinuationTypeDescriptor, continuationTypeForFunctionType, or mostGeneralContinuationType.  Most of them restrict labels or reified callers in L2; a reified caller becomes CONTINUATION().
- The Avail library has 57 occurrences of $[ across 13 modules, and most of them already mean labels.
- Bootstrap primitives: CreateContinuation ("$_@pc=_stack=_[_]caller=_"), ContinuationCaller, ContinuationFunction, ContinuationPC, ContinuationStackData, ContinuationStackPointer, ContinuationTypeToFunctionType, FunctionTypeToContinuationType.  Labels need their own accessors (caller, function, arguments); the pc, stack, and type-conversion primitives become continuation-only or label-only as appropriate.
- The L1 interpreter's push-label and L2's label creation build a Label.  L2_RESTART_CONTINUATION and the restart/exit primitives take labels.

Open decisions for Mark:
- Whether P_CreateContinuation survives.  Continuations "normally only created as a side effect of calling" argues against it.  If it stays, it can no longer be checked against a continuation type, so its checks become fully dynamic.  Find its library users first.
- Serialization: SerializerOperation entries for continuation types become label types, and compiled module caches (.repo) hold serialized types, so the repository format probably needs a version bump or cache invalidation.
- Sweep for code that compares labels by identity, reads a label's pc or stack, or relies on a restarted label being the running frame (the debugger, exception handling, fiber stack walks).
- Whether the debugger presents labels as data and continuations as frames.

Relation to the optimizer: avail-bjv models a label semantically as CreateLabel(caller, function, arguments), with the caller (L2SemanticCaller) as the value whose production needs reification.  After this split, producing a label shrinks to producing the caller plus one Label allocation: no L2_SAVE_ALL_AND_PC_TO_INT and no register dump.  That composes under inlining, since an inlined frame's caller is built from the enclosing frame's caller (avail-zv7, avail-6zs).
notes:
Rulings (Mark, 2026-11-20, follow-up):
- P_CreateContinuation stays.  The method "$_@pc=_stack=_[_]caller=_" is used only to synthesize the outermost base frame for an uncaught exception (Exceptions.avail, syntheticBase near line 2108).  It only creates an L1 continuation, and the debugger may need it for non-linear debug operations.  Its checks become dynamic, since the continuation type has no structure to check against.
- Serialization: bump the repository version when the serialization changes.  Continuations, labels, the single continuation type, and the whole lattice of label types must all be serializable.
- The existing debugger shows label-purposed continuations as values and also shows the frames; after the split, labels show as values and continuations as frames.
- Note: the library already spells a type "continuation" (syntheticBase declares "caller : continuation"); find what it is bound to and repoint it at CONTINUATION().
- Reminder for Mark: once everything is stable, check the debugger, exception handling, and fiber stack walks for problems (child bead).
Ruling (Mark, 2026-11-20, after avail-iel.3 landed in 5b92b20bc): labels need not capture arguments, neither as Avail objects (LabelDescriptor holds only caller and function) nor as L2 semantic values (the L2 label invocation is CreateLabel(caller, function), with no arguments tuple).  Label types are unchanged: they keep the function's parameter types and return type.  As of 5b92b20bc, label continuations already hold nil in every frame slot, AvailPushLabel no longer keeps arguments alive, and L2_VIRTUAL_CREATE_LABEL has no arguments operand.  The Restart_ primitive (restart with original arguments) is gone.
Ruling (Mark, 2026-11-20): label creation stays part of the block syntax with its own nybblecode (L1Ext_doPushLabel); it does not become a primitive (avail-iel.1 rejected).  After the split, L1Ext_doPushLabel builds a Label (caller, function).

title: Flow-sensitive escape for local variables, replacing the aliased-locals rule
description:
Replace the static aliased-locals rule in L1Translator with flow-sensitive escape, so that every local variable is elidable and its Create is forced only where something actually needs the variable object.

Today L1Translator.aliasedLocals scans the raw function for L1_doPushLocal / L1_doPushLastLocal of a local slot, and isElidableLocal excludes every such local from elision for the whole function, on every path, from the start (Variable_elision.md §Aliased locals).  An aliased local gets an eager, non-elidable Create at the head of the body, and every access uses the general L2_GET_VARIABLE / L2_GET_VARIABLE_CLEARING_IF_MUTABLE / L2_SET_VARIABLE instructions.

Goal (the epic's governing invariant): a variable whose Create is still postponed cannot be observed by anything; one whose Create has been emitted might be.  Before the Create, a Set folds into it as the new initial value and a Get becomes a move from that value.  After it, Set and Get are ordinary ordered memory operations.  Data flow alone forces the Create where something needs the variable object (a closure that is not inlined, a tuple, an argument to an invocation), so that point is the escape, flow-sensitively, and it survives regeneration because it lives in the graph.  On paths where the push never happens, the local stays elided.
design:
Read first: Variable_elision.md (all of it, especially §Aliased locals, §Escape, §Postponement, §Freezing) and the zv7 epic notes (VARIABLES, MERGES, ORDERING, and the "Landed in 809135bc1" block).

Ground as of 91475a30f:
- The freeze hook exists (809135bc1): L2_CREATE_CONTINUATION's 0..1 FREEZE edge, L2_ENTER_FREEZE ... L2_FINISH_FREEZE, created the first time a slot's Create/Set is still postponed at emission.  Placeholders (VariablePlaceholderDescriptor) are gone.  Elided-local reads fold to moves while the Create/Set is postponed; Create/Set folding happens in rewritePostponed at every block start (populateForMerge).
- Elided locals use L2_GET_ELIDABLE_LOCAL_VARIABLE / L2_SET_ELIDABLE_LOCAL_VARIABLE; aliased ones the general variable instructions.
- L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS and the escape-check machinery are gone (d94c7fbb6).

What changes:
- L1_doPushLocal / L1_doPushLastLocal of an elidable local reads the variable object itself, which forces the postponed Create (and any pending Set folded into it) at that point.  From there on, along that path, the variable has escaped: Gets and Sets must be the ordered, general forms, since invocations may read or write it.  Before it, or on paths that never push it, they stay elided.
- So "escaped" is per-path state carried in the manifest (for example: the Create is no longer postponed and the variable's register is live), not a per-function set.  At a merge where one predecessor has escaped and another has not, the merge emits the postponed Create on the edges lacking it (zv7 MERGES), and the merged state is escaped.
- The elidable Get/Set operations must decide at emission (emitTransformedInstruction) between the elided rewrite and the general form, based on that state; that may let one Get and one Set operation replace both pairs.
- Ordering (zv7 ORDERING): once escaped, accesses must not be reordered across invocations, L2_RETURN, or L2_GET_VARIABLE of possibly aliased variables.  Check what postponement and code motion currently assume about the elidable forms.
- Loops: a back edge whose loop body escapes a variable that was elided at loop entry needs the Create on entry (or a loop version), per zv7 LOOPS.  The simplest correct first step is to force the Create at the loop head when any path through the body escapes it; say which in the design.
- Delete aliasedLocals and isElidableLocal's alias test, and rewrite Variable_elision.md §Aliased locals (and §Escape) to describe flow-sensitive escape.

Open questions for Mark before implementing:
- Whether escape is tracked as its own manifest fact or inferred from the Create's postponement state.
- Loop handling: force at loop head vs. loop versioning now.

Benchmark: Mark's 1000-run benchmark was 116ms best at 91475a30f; compare after.

title: Narrow every Foldable primitive's guaranteed type over small enumeration products
description:
Generalize the enumeration-product narrowing that P_Addition, P_Subtraction,
P_Multiplication and P_Division do in returnTypeGuaranteedByVM: when every
argument type is an enumeration and the Cartesian product of their instance
sets has fewer than 100 combinations, the result type is the enumeration of
the primitive's outputs over those combinations.

Do it once, for every Foldable primitive, in a new final method on Primitive,
`guaranteedType(rawFunction, argumentTypes)`, which calls
returnTypeGuaranteedByVM and, when the arguments qualify, folds each
combination (via the Foldable path) and intersects the overridden answer with
the enumeration of the results.  Retarget all callers (about 54 references:
L1Translator, L2SimpleTranslator, L2ValueManifest, L2_RUN_INFALLIBLE_PRIMITIVE,
L2_INVOKE_CONSTANT_FUNCTION, the int arithmetic L2 ops, and the many
primitives that delegate to another primitive's guarantee) at guaranteedType.
The 88 overrides stay as they are, and the four arithmetic primitives drop
their hand-written product code.

Motivating example: TEST "double representation reinterpretation" calls
the bits-reinterpretation primitive on an enumeration of doubles; its
guarantee is the full i64 range, so the chunk keeps a type test the
enumeration of results would have made unnecessary.

Questions for design:
- A combination whose fold fails (primitive failure or exception) must make
  the narrowing abandon, or exclude that combination, depending on whether the
  primitive can fail; decide which.
- Folding at type-computation time must stay cheap and side-effect free;
  Foldable already promises that, but confirm the threshold and that folding
  doesn't allocate unboundedly (e.g. huge tuples).
- Visibility: callers outside Primitive should not reach
  returnTypeGuaranteedByVM directly.  Kotlin's `protected` is subclass-only,
  which fits if every cross-primitive delegation also moves to
  guaranteedType (it should, to get the narrowing).  Check whether Kotlin
  permits a subclass to call a protected member through a receiver of type
  Primitive; if not, an alternative is an abstract inner hook object or a
  @PublishedApi-style internal naming convention.
notes:
Visibility ruling (Mark, in session): Kotlin's protected is not a usable
restriction here; do not rely on it.

Candidate pattern: a capability token.  Give returnTypeGuaranteedByVM an extra
parameter of a type that only Primitive can construct, e.g. a final class
nested in Primitive with a private constructor and one private instance.
Subclasses can name the type in their override signatures but cannot obtain
an instance, so only Primitive.guaranteedType can call the override.  A
primitive that delegates to another primitive's guarantee must then call
guaranteedType, which is what it should do anyway to get the narrowing.
The cost is one ignored parameter in each of the 88 overrides.

title: Interpreter-free helper entry methods in JVM chunks
description:
Generated JVM chunks get interpreter-free helper entry methods, alongside runChunk, for code paths that must run outside normal execution.  The driving use is the freeze subgraph: when a continuation built by L2 code is made immutable or shared, the chunk's freeze helper is invoked with that continuation and the entry offset, creates the variables of any elided locals, writes them into the continuation's slots, and switches it to DefaultL1Chunk at its fallback entry point.

Rulings (2026-11-18):
- Implement this now rather than later, since retrofitting would rip up decisions about the interpreter; passing the continuation in and out of a helper method avoids involving the interpreter at all.
- Dispatch within a helper uses the same offset lookupswitch mechanism as runChunk.

This should also suit inlining, with or without an L2-friendly multi-level continuation that freezes into several L1-friendly ones.

title: Uniform variables and freeze hook for full inlining
description:
Replace placeholder-based variable elision with uniform variables plus a freeze hook, as groundwork for full inlining (closures passed to known flow-control methods and primitives, continuations for loop detection).

Goal: there is nothing special about local variables.  Every variable, local or explicitly created, is a Create plus Sets and Gets, and those commute by ordinary rules.  The governing invariant: a variable whose Create is still postponed cannot be observed by anything; one whose Create has been emitted might be.  Before the Create, a Set folds into it as the new initial value and a Get becomes a move from that value (nil-ness decided by its type restriction).  After it, Set and Get are ordinary ordered memory operations.  Data flow alone forces the Create where something needs the variable object (a closure not inlined, a tuple, an argument), so that point is the escape, flow-sensitively, surviving regeneration because it lives in the graph.

This replaces the static aliased-locals rule in L1Translator (aliasedLocals / isElidedLocal), which is the interim fix that keeps aliased locals correct.

Children: start with a design doc under avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/ covering the points in the notes, then split implementation beads from it.
notes:
Ideas and rulings from the design discussion (2026-11-16/17):

FREEZE HOOK
- In practice only label creation (and the AvailDebugger) makes a continuation immutable/shared; always with an interpreter present.  Inlining control structures makes labels rarer still.  A shared fiber does not share its current continuation: the fiber is the scope boundary, and primitives never expose a running fiber's continuation (like a Smalltalk Process whose stack is nil while active).  The inter-fiber stack-extraction mechanism reifies the examined fiber under controlled circumstances and is currently unused.
- Hook shape: L2_RETURN_FROM_REIFICATION_HANDLER gains a jump target, taken when the continuation is frozen (makeImmutable/makeShared).  The subgraph there runs ordinary L2 code to turn the L2-friendly continuation into an L1-friendly one, creating any variables still postponed and switching the continuation's chunk to the DefaultL1Chunk.  Postponed side-effect-free work (Creates, closure creations, boxing, inlined frames) sinks into it as the coldest tier: hot path, reification path, freeze path.
- The freeze subgraph may not invoke, reify, take interrupts, or read the interpreter's arguments or return value.  A JVMTranslator extension can emit it as its own JVM method with no interpreter; a loadInterpreter() there is a code generation error.
- Install the canonical state by indirection (IndirectionDescriptor), so existing references to the continuation see it.  The hook must run before the makeImmutable/makeShared traversal reads the continuation's contents.
- Two representations: a mutable continuation built by L2 is L2-friendly only, with chunk-private slot and register-dump layout; nothing reads it as L1 without first freezing it.  A single L2 continuation can stand for a chain of L1 continuations (inlined frames) and expands into that chain during the freeze.  Be careful about an embedded P_CatchException frame (handler markers); it will be tricky to get right.

VARIABLES
- Every local has a Create somewhere on the path from the method start to the end of the freeze subgraph, except after L1_doPushLastLocal, which writes nil into the slot and relieves the debt.
- VariablePlaceholderDescriptor, ContinuationDescriptor.createElidedVariables, SaveAll's dirtyLocals/dirtyLocalIndices handling, and L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS become unnecessary; probably the *_UNESCAPED_* instruction variants too (one Get and one Set that rewrite against a postponed Create, else general).
- Closures have no identity: their creation can be postponed, omitted, or repeated.  Only captured variables need one identity, which the single Create instruction instance provides even in the freeze subgraph.
- Agglomerate a variable's value into the synonym with a new kind of semantic value, e.g. L2VariableValueSemanticValue(semanticVariable), so the value of a variable participates in ordinary synonym and ordering machinery.

LOOPS (loop versioning)
- First loop version: assume every variable still elided on first reaching the loop stays postponed.  If at the end of generating a version all are still postponed, jump back to that version (best fixed point).  Otherwise create a new loop version to jump back to, passing the variables created so far to its top.  Repeat.

MERGES
- A variable created on some incoming edges but not others is the general case of a value computed on some predecessors only: the merge emits the postponed Create (or the computation of the value to write) on the edges lacking a live value.
- At each polymorphic lookup-and-invoke, the L1 translation introduces safety variable versioning: whatever the inlined blocks do to a variable, a fenced move brings it to a common variable/value version at the merge at the end of the L1 call site.  Example: If-then-else whose arms are [x := foo();] and [x := bar(); x++; x := x + 10;].

ORDERING
- Created variables are ordered only by hidden-variable effects, so invokes, L2_RETURN and L2_GET_VARIABLE must declare their reads/writes before any pass reorders more aggressively than postponement.

FINDINGS TO CARRY (current placeholder mechanism, until replaced)
- Create/Set fusion (L2_SET_UNESCAPED_LOCAL_VARIABLE.rewritePostponed) only runs via L2ValueManifest.rewriteAllPostponed, whose sole caller is populateForMerge.  Commit 891911547 removed the per-block call in the postponement regeneration.  So Create x := nil; Set x := v is usually emitted unfused (e.g. Tuples:136).  Variable_elision.md §Postponement still describes the fusion as happening in any regeneration.
- Unverified: a pending Set stacked on a pending Create reaching L2_SAVE_ALL_AND_PC_TO_INT: aboutToAdd skips the Create (nil initial value) for dirtyLocals, and the fall-through edge binds the Create's output to the placeholder constant while the Set still reads it; forcing that Set on the fall-through path would trip its init assert, and an immutable continuation would create the local unassigned.

INLINING DIRECTION
- Inline when an invocation passes a freshly built closure (lexically enclosing local data, perhaps variables), a continuation (extends loop detection), or the called operation is a known (perhaps polymorphic) flow-control primitive.  Later, L1 scans of called functions that take closures capturing locals can make inlining decisions as part of the same analysis.
Update (2026-11-17, avail-9dm): regenerateForPostponement is gone; the Get rewrites now live in emitTransformedInstruction of both unescaped Get operations, the postponement phases are plain BySemanticValue regenerations, and forcePostponedWritesToLocals was removed (postponed Sets now only target elided, unaliased locals, which nothing else can see).  Variable_elision.md §Postponement now states that Create/Set fusion happens only at control flow merges, so the fusion finding above is documented behavior rather than a doc error; reducing at postponement time remains an option.
Update (d94c7fbb6, avail-jfk): L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS, emitCheckLocals, the escape-testing CallSiteHelper junctions, mightMakeEscapedVariableShared, and Primitive.Flag.MightMakeEscapedVariableShared are already gone; the redesign need not remove them.  Variable_elision.md §Escape states why an elided local cannot escape while its L2 code runs (a freeze switches the continuation to DefaultL1Chunk).
Ruling (2026-11-17): the freeze subgraph is one instance of a more general pattern, an alternate entry point that a chunk exposes for each frame it may have reified.  Inlining a P_CatchException call could create a similar subgraph acting as a catcher entry point.  During P_RaiseException, after reifying the stack, the runtime invokes that entry point in each frame's chunk to ask whether the frame wants to catch the exception or run a finally block.  The same walk can collect a summary of the stack trace frame by frame as frames are exited, so the stack need not be made immutable unless the full trace is actually used at the catch site; there, a reification can collect the remainder.  See the exception-handling child bead.

Also from the same discussion: stripping the escape checks (the whole aliased-but-not-yet-escaped space) cost essentially nothing in Mark's 1000-run benchmark (118-121ms before, 123ms after), so that year of experiments amounted to a near-null optimization; the real wins are expected from inlining.
Landed in 809135bc1 (2026-11-19), superseding parts of the notes above:
- The freeze edge hangs off L2_CREATE_CONTINUATION (a 0..1 L2PcVectorOperand,
  Purpose.FREEZE), not L2_RETURN_FROM_REIFICATION_HANDLER.  It is added the
  first time a slot's Create/Set is still postponed at emission, and kept
  thereafter; later regenerations regenerate the freeze block.
- Freeze subgraph: L2_ENTER_FREEZE (restores registers from the dump) ...
  L2_FINISH_FREEZE (frameAtPutAll, return).  JVM: freeze(continuation) method,
  lookupswitch on RegisterDumpDescriptor FREEZE_OFFSET (-1 = no-op).  SaveAll
  reserves dump room at JVM-generation time.  No IndirectionDescriptor is
  used: createElidedVariables runs freeze in place, then switches the
  continuation to DefaultL1Chunk at the dump's fallback entry point.
- Placeholders are gone.  Elided-local reads now fold to moves while the
  Create/Set is postponed (the check was hasSemanticValue, now
  hasLiveSemanticValue BOXED).  Create/Set folding happens in
  rewritePostponed at every block start (populateForMerge).
- Still open for the epic's goal: the static aliasedLocals / isElidableLocal
  rule in L1Translator, replaced by flow-sensitive escape (data flow forcing
  the Create).  No bead exists for that yet.
- Known latent issue: SaveAll's dump records REENTRY_FROM_REIFIED_CALL as the
  L1 fallback even for interrupt reification (L1Translator ~1843 uses RESUME).
  A frozen interrupt continuation of a function with locals would resume L1
  at the wrong entry.  Fix: take the fallback from the reference target's
  L2_ENTER_L2_CHUNK.entryPointOffsetInDefaultChunk.
2026-11-20: the flow-sensitive escape work (replacing aliasedLocals / isElidableLocal) is now avail-zv7.5.

title: Define producibility recursively, and rebuild self-describing values on demand
description:
Define whether a semantic value can be produced recursively, and let the manifest rebuild self-describing values on demand.

A value is producible if a register in its synonym holds it, if it is a constant, if it has a postponed instruction whose inputs are all producible, or if it describes its own computation (an L2SemanticPrimitiveInvocation, a tag, a variant id) and every argument is producible.  So a primitive invocation over a semantic slot that cannot be produced cannot be produced either.  Today a primitive invocation counts as unproducible unless it is constant or carries a postponed instruction; nothing is rebuilt on demand.

With rebuilding on demand, a manifest need not keep a postponed instruction for a value it can rebuild.  Postponed instructions would remain only where placement matters, keeping manifests smaller.

Audit the optimizations that probe for related semantic values: each one that emits a read must ask whether the value can be produced, not whether it is known.  A probe that uses only the restriction is fine as it is.  Some probes already ask about producibility.
design:
Constraints identified when the bead was filed (2026-11-14):
- Only a primitive that cannot fail and has no side effects can be rebuilt on demand.  A fallible primitive needs a failure path, so it cannot be inserted wherever its value is read.
- Rebuilding gives up placement.  A value rebuilt at each read may be computed separately on several paths, which postponement exists to avoid.  Producibility is about existence; postponement is about placement.
- The recursion terminates, since an invocation's arguments come before it; remember each answer to keep it cheap.
- Background: a value in post-phi data with no producer is harmless.  In a complete graph nothing reads it, and regeneration cannot create a new reader.  Its restriction is still useful knowledge.  See the closing notes of avail-ezf.5 and avail-ezf.1.
- Design it alongside avail-1ww (fold populated into live), since both redefine what the manifest answers when asked for a value.  It also bears on avail-9dm (whether the postponement phases are vestigial).
notes:
Ground as of 2026-11-14 (commit 4ccaf943b, avail-1ww landed): populated is folded into live.  The manifest's register queries are now hasLiveSemanticValue, hasLiveSemanticValueInAnyKind, equivalentLiveSemanticValue, and getDefinitions (every register of the kind holding the class).  "Producible" is the third question this bead adds beside known and live; see Value_manifest.md §Data model.Known and live.
Traps found the hard way: an argument introduced as an anchor starts at its default restriction (often top) until something narrows it, and binding an invocation propagates its class's restriction to its arguments.  agglomerateSynonym now narrows before binding, and the deep manifest check asserts no side-effectless invocation is restricted to top.  Rebuilding values on demand will add new binding paths; keep that order.
To exercise: shrink the OptimizationLevel countdowns to 10, set shouldSanityCheck and deepManifestDebugCheck, and run AvailTest (Mark stress-tests by running the Avail tests hundreds of times; a regression appeared only after 470 runs).

title: Run L2 optimization asynchronously on the executor instead of blocking the triggering thread
description:
Run L2 (re)optimization as a separate task on the executor's thread pool, instead of synchronously on the thread whose countdown reached zero.  The triggering fiber keeps running the slower code it already has and keeps making progress; the optimized chunk is plugged in whenever it is ready.

Today the work is synchronous.  L2_DECREMENT_COUNTER_AND_REOPTIMIZE_ON_ZERO.decrement (and L2SimpleExecutableChunk, around line 163) calls OptimizationLevel.optimize(code, interpreter) inline, then switches the interpreter to the new chunk.  The fiber is stalled for the whole of the optimization.

The executor (AvailRuntime.executor, fed by WorkStealingQueue<AvailTask>) already runs tasks other than fiber execution, so an optimization task fits.  Three problems must be solved:

1. Safe points.  Optimization tasks must interleave correctly with safe-point processing (AvailRuntime.whenSafePointDo and interpreterSurplus).  We need to decide whether an optimization task counts as an interpreter task, which must drain before a safe point, or as something else.  We also need to decide when installing the chunk (setStartingChunkAndReoptimizationCountdown) is safe relative to safe points and to concurrent invalidation of the code's dependencies.

2. The countdown protocol.  A function queued for optimization must keep decrementing its countdown past zero.  When the optimized chunk is installed, the overshoot (how far below zero it went) offsets the new countdown, so the invocations made while waiting are credited to the new chunk.  Only the decrement that reaches exactly zero may enqueue the task.

3. Work-giving.  We *want* another thread to take the optimization task while the identifying thread keeps running.  WorkStealingQueue only moves work when a thread runs dry and steals, so a task offered to the busy thread's own subqueue may sit there until that thread finishes its fiber.  The queue may need a "work-giving" path that hands a task to an idle or less loaded subqueue, or wakes a thief to take it promptly.
design:
Ground to read first:
- interpreter/levelTwo/operation/L2_DECREMENT_COUNTER_AND_REOPTIMIZE_ON_ZERO.kt, decrement() and its JVM translation.  After optimizing it jumps straight into the new chunk via interpreterRunChunkMethod; the asynchronous version instead falls through and keeps running the current chunk.
- CompiledCodeDescriptor.decrementCountdownToReoptimize (the companion function): today Long.MAX_VALUE means never reoptimize, and <= 0 means already being reoptimized, so the countdown is NOT decremented below zero.  Change this so it keeps decrementing below zero while queued, without colliding with MAX_VALUE and without letting a second caller see "exactly zero".
- CompiledCodeDescriptor.o_SetStartingChunkAndReoptimizationCountdown: today it installs the chunk, then set()s the countdown.  It needs to become an atomic read-and-adjust (new countdown + overshoot, clamped to stay positive), with the existing comment about other threads running the new chunk under a negative countdown re-examined.
- o_DecreaseCountdownToReoptimizeFromPoll and the fallback-lookup reset (countdownResetAfterEnoughFallbackLookups): these only touch a positive countdown, so check how they interact with a queued, negative one.
- AvailRuntime: executor, execute(AvailTask), whenSafePointDo, interpreterSurplus, and the postponed safe-point task queue.
- utility/WorkStealingQueue.kt: per-interpreter LeftistHeap subqueues, stealing, and idlePermits/signal.

Open questions to settle with Mark before implementing:
- What priority do optimization tasks get relative to fiber tasks?
- If the code is invalidated (a method definition changes) while its optimization is queued or running, the result must be discarded, not installed.  How is that detected: a generation stamp on the code, or the chunk's own validity?
- Must OptimizationLevel / L1Translator / L2Optimizer use only the interpreter it is given, or do they rely on the triggering fiber's interpreter state (interpreter.function, current chunk)?  The task runs on a different interpreter.
- Should the same mechanism apply to the L2Simple path (L2SimpleExecutableChunk)?
- Does work-giving belong in WorkStealingQueue in general (an offer-to-other-subqueue operation), or only for optimization tasks?
notes:
Mark's rulings (2026-11-13):
- Priority: an optimization task is urgent.  Give it a very high AvailTask priority, above fiber tasks.
- Invalidation needs no special handling.  An optimization task runs while safe points are held off, and method definitions only change during a safe point.  A safe point can run while the task waits in the queue, but nothing is prepared before the task runs, so it optimizes against the methods as they are when it runs.  Drop the open question about discarding an invalidated result.
- The cheap translation stays synchronous.  Building the L2Simple chunk (OptimizationLevel.UNOPTIMIZED, L2SimpleTranslator) costs little and breaks even after a few invocations.  Note: the L2Simple chunk's own countdown site (L2SimpleExecutableChunk, around line 163) calls SIMPLE_TRANSLATION.optimize, which is the expensive L1Translator translation to L2/JVM.  So that site appears to belong in the asynchronous scheme along with L2_DECREMENT_COUNTER_AND_REOPTIMIZE_ON_ZERO.  Confirm with Mark.
- Work-giving becomes a general WorkStealingQueue operation, usable beyond optimization, for example by the fork primitives.
- Running without a fiber is a benefit.  The optimizer gets its own interpreter with no fiber.  Today folding has to save and restore the triggering fiber's interpreter state; in its own task there is no fiber state to protect, so that save and restore can go away.  The open question about relying on the triggering fiber's interpreter state is answered.
- Trap for the countdown protocol: each OptimizationLevel.optimize calls code.countdownToReoptimize(countdown) BEFORE translating, not when the chunk is installed.  The overshoot offset has to replace that early reset.
Confirmed by Mark: SIMPLE_TRANSLATION.optimize (reached from the L2Simple chunk's countdown) is where the optimization task is queued.  Until it completes, invocations keep running the L2Simple chunk.

title: mergeValueClasses forwards the winner to the loser, dropping the merged state
description:
L2ValueManifest.mergeValueClasses(winner, loser) stores the merged ValueState
under winner and then calls forwardClass(loser, winner), with the arguments
swapped relative to forwardClass(winner, loser).  forwardClass removes the
