title: Verify which post-phi witnesses survive without postponed instructions
description:
Determine which values in a captured post-phi data have a witness that
survives without postponed instructions, and therefore whether leaving
postponed instructions out of PostPhiData (L2ValueManifest.extractPostPhiData)
loses any value.  The old design doc argued that every synonym is witnessed
by a register, a constant restriction, synonymy with a witnessed value,
presence on every incoming edge, or a self-describing semantic value
(primitive invocation, tag, variant id), so a postponement is never the only
witness.  That has not been checked against the manifest's postponed
information: some witness kinds may in fact be supplied only by a postponed
instruction.  Carrying postponed information unnecessarily would be harmless
apart from manifest size, so the cost of a wrong "not needed" is higher than
the cost of a wrong "needed".

The design's text (from the retired
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 5) is
in this bead's design field.  If the argument holds, describe the witness
invariant in avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Post_phi_data.md; avail-ezf.1
then asserts it.
design:
## 5. Witnesses, and why postponements need not be captured

Every synonym in a `postPhiData` needs a **witness**: something that will
make the value producible again when the information is replayed. A synonym with
no witness is a value that is known, unproducible, and reachable by anything
that goes looking — the exact pathology this whole effort has been chasing.

The admissible witnesses are:

1. an instruction in the block that writes it, replayed by processing the block
   in the ordinary way;
2. a constant restriction, which the implicit postponed constant move satisfies;
3. synonymy with a value that is itself witnessed, which produces it by the
   implicit move;
4. presence in every incoming edge, witnessed by the predecessors;
5. a semantic value that describes its own computation — an
   `L2SemanticPrimitiveInvocation`, a tag, a variant id — for which a fresh
   instruction can be synthesized on demand.

An earlier draft of this design also captured postponed instructions, on the
grounds that a postponement is the only witness for a value that has floated
out of its block. That is not so, and the four arguments against it are worth
recording, since the temptation will recur.

**Ordering.** SSA puts a write before its reads, so nothing in the block can
observe a value before the instruction that produces it. The concern that a
hoisted fact would be visible "too early" only bites for observers that are not
reads, and each of those turns out to be safe.

**Constant folding** operates only on constants, so the implicit postponed
constant move is a sufficient witness — witness (2). Nothing needs to be
carried.

**Primitive output re-strengthening** operates on restrictions — the constant
if it is known, otherwise the type — and restrictions are exactly what the
`postPhiData` carries. It never consults a register.

**Primitive invocation reuse** has two cases, and both are witnessed:

- there is a register holding an equivalent invocation, in which case the
  synonym is simply extended with the new semantic value; or
- there is no register, in which case the synonym is still augmented and a
  *fresh* postponed instruction is added that runs the primitive — witness (5).

The second case is the interesting one, because the freshly postponed
instruction may be emitted at a point earlier than wherever the original
producer ended up, which can be far downstream. That is harmless: when
regeneration eventually reaches the later original instruction, `unaryPlus`
finds the synonym already present in the manifest with a populated register,
and degrades to a move.

So a postponement is a statement about *placement*, not about existence. Every
value the manifest knows is producible from a register in its synonym, from a
constant, or by re-running the computation its own semantic value describes,
and all three survive without being transported.

A related property of postponement, independent of this design but worth
keeping in view: **a postponed instruction's reads are not uses of its
inputs.** Dead code elimination walks the instruction graph, and a postponed
instruction is not in it, so an input read only by a postponement looks unused.
It may be postponed in turn, but it must not be dropped, or the postponement
becomes unemittable.
notes: Obsolete (2026-11-14).  Leaving postponed instructions out of PostPhiData does no harm.  In a complete graph, every emitted read has already forced its producer to be emitted, so a post-phi value with no witness has no readers.  Regeneration starts from fresh manifests, carries no postponed instructions across, and only regenerates the old graph's instructions, so no new reader can appear.  Such an entry is still a useful fact about what the value would be.  The old argument's witness 5 (rebuilding a self-describing value on demand) is not implemented: a primitive invocation counts as unproducible unless it is constant or carries a postponed instruction.
close_reason: Obsolete: a post-phi value with no witness has no readers, and regeneration cannot create one

title: Escape checks for locals shared through inlined primitives
description:
Variable elision assumes a created local stays unshared and reactor-free unless something observable happens, and L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS is emitted only after non-inlined calls (CallSiteHelper.AfterCallNoCheckTestEscapes) and after writes to literal variables (L1_doSetLiteral / emitSetVariableOffRamp).  Calls that are inlined or run as primitives in L2 take paths without that check (e.g. AfterCallNoCheckNoEscapes).  Determine whether that leaves a gap, and close it.

Cases to examine:
- An inlined primitive that can make an argument (or a component of one) shared, e.g. writing a tuple containing a created local into a shared variable, or passing it to another fiber.
- The variable read/write primitives (get, set, clear, atomic update) inlined on some variable SV, when a created local V is reachable from SV's contents: a write of <V> into a shared SV shares V.
- A local that escaped (was created and captured) but is not shared: L2_SET_UNESCAPED_LOCAL_VARIABLE remains postponable after the escape, and is forced only at L2_INVOKE / L2_INVOKE_CONSTANT_FUNCTION / L2_RETURN.  An inlined primitive that reads the variable through another path (a tuple, an outer) could observe a stale value.

Possible remedies: emit the escape check after primitives that may share their arguments (a primitive flag would say which), stop inlining the variable-write primitives, or force postponed Sets of escaped locals before any instruction that writes global state.  Add a test for each case that is reachable.  The design is described in avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Variable_elision.md.
notes:
Correction to the third case (escaped-but-unshared locals with postponed Sets): a postponed L2_SET_UNESCAPED_LOCAL_VARIABLE only survives for a local that has already been created, since a Set reaching a still-postponed Create merges into it.  L2_INVOKE, L2_INVOKE_CONSTANT_FUNCTION, and L2_RETURN force every surviving postponed Set (forcePostponedWritesToLocals) in their regenerateForPostponement, so invokes are covered.  What remains to examine: the instructions that run primitives inline without forcing them, namely L2_RUN_INFALLIBLE_PRIMITIVE, L2_TRY_PRIMITIVE, and primitive-specific generated code (e.g. an inlined variable read or write), plus L2_INVOKE_INVALID_MESSAGE_RESULT_FUNCTION.  Also note the forcing lives in regenerateForPostponement, so it happens only in the explicit postponement phases; if another BySemanticValue regeneration carries a postponed Set to an invoke, nothing forces it there (see avail-9dm).
Narrowed further: the mechanism for primitives already exists.  Primitive.Flag.MightMakeEscapedVariableShared (Primitive.mightMakeEscapedVariableShared) marks primitives that can share a local or give it a reactor (P_SetValue, P_Fork, the atomic variable primitives, P_AddWriteReactor, and about sixty others), and the general inlining path passes it to CallSiteHelper.useAnswer, which then routes to the ...TestEscapes junctions and emits L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS.  What remains:
- Primitive-specific generators that answer with useAnswer(..., false) although the primitive carries the flag.  Concrete suspect: P_AtomicCompareAndSwap's special generation answers false on both its success and failure paths, yet a successful swap writes newValue into a possibly shared variable, which shares anything reachable from newValue (including a created local).  P_GetValue and P_GetClearing also answer false, which is right for a read.
- Whether every primitive that needs the flag has it.
- Postponed L2_SET_UNESCAPED_LOCAL_VARIABLE instructions are not forced before L2_RUN_INFALLIBLE_PRIMITIVE or L2_TRY_PRIMITIVE, even for flagged primitives.  Determine whether a flagged primitive can observe an escaped local's pending value through another path before the Set is emitted.
Since b7aadbfb1 (avail-9dm): a local whose variable object is ever pushed (L1_doPushLocal / L1_doPushLastLocal) is aliased and never elided; it is created eagerly and accessed only with L2_GET_VARIABLE / L2_GET_VARIABLE_CLEARING_IF_MUTABLE / L2_SET_VARIABLE, which handle shared variables and reactors themselves, and it is excluded from L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS.  An elided local's variable object can then never reach a primitive, a tuple, or another variable's contents, so the cases above may no longer be reachable.  Remaining question: can an elided local still become shared or reactive at all (only via reification of its frame), and is the Check after non-inlined calls still needed for it?  Likely closable after that check.  avail-zv7 removes L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS entirely.
close_reason: Unreachable since b7aadbfb1: every case needs the local's variable object, which only L1_doPushLocal/L1_doPushLastLocal expose, and a pushed local is aliased, never elided, and accessed only through the general variable instructions. A frozen continuation of an elided frame resumes in L1 (createElidedVariables switches to DefaultL1Chunk), so no L2 code observes a shared or reactive elided local.

title: Decide whether the explicit postponement phases are vestigial
description:
Question: are the explicit POSTPONE_CONDITIONALLY_USED_VALUES_1/2/3 phases (OptimizationPhase, L2Optimizer.postponeConditionallyUsedValues) still needed, or are they vestigial now that postponement happens during most BySemanticValue regenerations?

What the explicit pass does that other regenerations do not: it calls regenerateForPostponement() on each instruction instead of the ordinary transform.  Overrides of regenerateForPostponement exist in L2_MOVE, L2_NOP, L2_PHI, L2_INVOKE, L2_INVOKE_CONSTANT_FUNCTION, L2_RETURN, L2_CREATE_VARIABLE, L2_GET_UNESCAPED_LOCAL_VARIABLE, and L2_GET_AND_CLEAR_IF_MUTABLE_UNESCAPED_LOCAL_VARIABLE.  Notably the variable-elision Get rewrite (a Get reached by a postponed Create/Set/Get becomes a move plus a jump to the success or failure edge) and the forcing of postponed Sets at invokes and returns (forcePostponedWritesToLocals) live there.

What already happens in any BySemanticValue regeneration: L2Instruction.aboutToAdd (e.g. L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS dropping locals whose creation is still postponed), L2ValueManifest's rewritePostponed (Create+Set and Set+Set merging), and the instructionWasAdded handling of postponed creations at L2_SAVE_ALL_AND_PC_TO_INT.

Work: inventory each regenerateForPostponement override, decide whether its effect belongs in the ordinary regeneration path (or in another pass), move it, and remove the explicit phases (and their REMOVE_DEAD_CODE_AFTER_POSTPONEMENTS companions) if nothing is left.  Check: the full avail test suite, plus comparing L2 listings for a few representative chunks before and after (no loss of elision).
notes:
Correctness angle: forcePostponedWritesToLocals runs only from the regenerateForPostponement overrides of L2_INVOKE, L2_INVOKE_CONSTANT_FUNCTION, and L2_RETURN, so outside the explicit phases nothing forces a postponed Set at an invoke.  Folding the explicit phases into ordinary regeneration must keep that forcing (and avail-kb5 may want it at primitive-running instructions as well).
Ground changed by avail-gtb (commit 1850884a6, 2026-11-15):
- Postponement now elides some instructions entirely (L2Instruction.canBeElidedFromPostponement): moves, constant moves, box/unbox, and an L2_RUN_INFALLIBLE_PRIMITIVE whose result names its invocation.  Such values live only as known members of their class and are produced on demand by L2Generator.ensureDefinedOrEmitMove*.  See Value_manifest.md §Postponed instructions.Elided postponement and §Data model.Producible.
- canBePostponed is now a function of the manifest; infallible primitives delegate to Primitive.canBePostponed(arguments, manifest).  Side-effectless primitives are postponed again (LATEST_RETURN_VALUE left their write mask), so the postponement phases now move far more instructions than before.
- populateForMerge keeps values producible on every edge, so elided invocations survive merges without the phases' help.
- The stale "DEBUGGING: Disabled" notes on these phases were removed; the phases do run.
This bead's answer feeds avail-bjv's open question about whether postponed pseudo-primitives get the same motility as placeholders.
close_reason: Explicit postponement passes removed; Get rewrites run at translation and in every BySemanticValue regeneration; aliased locals no longer elided

title: Widen trial division's fast path to 64-bit bounds
description: Trial division's fast path (trial division factorization of_«,⁇from_»?«,⁇to_»?, Late Math.avail) was specialized to search bounds below 2^31 - 60, from when L2 had only 32-bit integer registers. L2 now has 64-bit registers, so widen the bounds to 2^63 - 60, letting the loop index stay unboxed for every number below about 2^126. Add a test that factors a product in [2^62..2^63 - 60), whose square root needs the widened path.

title: L2: compute masked and modular products without big integers
description:
Goal: let the L2 optimizer compute modular products in machine words, so Avail code gets fast modular arithmetic just by writing the natural expression, without asking for it.

1. Masked products. When L2 sees ((a × b) bit∧ m), where m = 2^k − 1 for some k ≤ 64 and a and b are known integers (not necessarily small), substitute ((a bit∧ m) × (b bit∧ m)) bit∧ m, where the multiply is the low-limb (wrapping) 64-bit multiply. The low k bits of a product depend only on the low k bits of its factors, so the result is exact, and no big integer is created however large a, b, or their true product is. The same holds for the masked operands of + and −, and chains of them under one mask.

2. Remainders of products. When L2 sees ((a × b) mod n), with 0 < n ≤ 2^63 and a and b known to lie in [0..n) (or reducible into it), compute the product's remainder without big-integer arithmetic: form the 128-bit product (Math.multiplyHigh and the low 64-bit multiply; Math.unsignedMultiplyHigh for unsigned operands), then reduce it modulo n. The JVM has no 128-by-64 division, so the reduction needs its own routine (for example a two-step long division on 64-bit halves, or a precomputed reciprocal per modulus when n is loop-invariant).

Motivation: the library's primality code (Late Math.avail) spends its time in modular exponentiation. "_^_mod_" and "_is a strong probable prime to base_" square values below the modulus and reduce them. For moduli up to 2^64, those products need up to 128 bits and currently become big integers. Sinclair's 7-base Miller-Rabin test for [2^32..2^64] does about 7 × 64 such squarings per call, which dominates the "primality tests" test. FJ32_256's hash ((h >> 16) bit⊕ h) × 0x45d9f3b followed by a mask is the masked-product case.

Notes:
- Both rewrites apply only when the operands' static types (restrictions) prove the preconditions: integer operands, and for the remainder, a positive modulus no larger than 2^63 and operands within [0..n).
- The results must be exactly what the unfused Avail operations would compute; this is a strength reduction, not an approximation.
- Avail tests should compare the fused results against the generic path on values chosen around the boundaries (k = 63 and 64; moduli near 2^32, 2^62, and 2^63; operands of n − 1).

title: Stop the I/O tests from flushing the whole drive
description:
Problem: the I/O tests spend most of each test run waiting on whole-drive flushes. Closing a file writer synchronizes it (Close_ on a file writer calls Synchronize_, in File Iterators.avail), and synchronizing reaches P_FileSync, whose FileChannel.force is fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC) on macOS: a flush of the drive's entire write cache, about 16-20 ms each, serialized across the drive. While one is in flight, every metadata-changing call on the volume (create, chmod, unlink, rename) waits for it.

Evidence:
- A standalone benchmark on the repository's volume: create, chmod, and unlink took about 0.02-0.08 ms alone, about the same beside concurrent fsync, and about 20.8 ms each beside concurrent F_FULLFSYNC.
- The workbench's primitive statistics: P_FileOpen averaged 19 ms and P_FileSetPermissions 9 ms, while read-only P_FileMetadata averaged 0.77 ms.
- A traced warm pass: tests other than the I/O tests finished by about 134 ms, while the I/O suite ran until about 405 ms. Groups of I/O tests finished at the same instant (for example four at 118.4 ms, three at 248.296 ms), consistent with flushes completing together. Pass times varied from about 400 to 1,000 ms.

Sources of flushes in the tests:
- The I/O suite's setup ("Before running I/O test suite" in File Test Utilities.avail) closes two writers (abracadabra.txt, scratch.txt), gating every I/O test behind about 54 ms of flushing.
- "a private copy of abracadabra.txt" writes each copy through a file writer, so each of the dozen access-rights tests that uses one pays a full flush. These private copies exist so that those tests can run concurrently without interfering.
- Four tests synchronize deliberately: file iterator (refresh/synchronize), (alignment), (scattered write), and file(round trip) (the last is inside a block comment in IO Tests.avail and does not run).

Options:
1. In the tests: create the private copies and the setup's files without a file writer (for example with the library's file copy, or by opening and closing a channel without a writer), so they never synchronize. Only the tests that test synchronization would still flush.
2. In the library: stop Close_ on a file writer from synchronizing, leaving durability to an explicit Synchronize_. This changes a documented behavior, and callers relying on close-means-durable would need an explicit Synchronize_.
3. The FFM file layer (avail-rlc) offers cheaper sync levels (drive vs. durable), which removes most of the cost at its source.

Related: avail-rlc (FFM file operations and sync levels), avail-6s8 (file primitives no longer block interpreter threads while they wait).
notes:
Ruling (Mark, 2026-11-10): give up on F_FULLFSYNC.  Synchronize_ means plain
fsync (data and metadata reach the drive; not power-loss durable on macOS).
A durable level may be added later if needed, and its documentation must say
plainly that on macOS it is a whole-filesystem (whole-drive) flush, not a
per-file one.

Chosen approach (replaces options 1-3 as the primary fix):

- java.io.FileDescriptor.sync() is plain fsync on every Unix including macOS
  (io_util_md.h: #define IO_Sync fsync; no macOS special case), while
  FileChannel.force is always F_FULLFSYNC on local macOS volumes, whatever
  its metaData flag.  On Windows both are FlushFileBuffers.
- AsynchronousFileChannel on Unix is SimpleAsynchronousFileChannelImpl: a
  thread pool doing blocking pread/pwrite.  Replacing it loses no real async
  I/O.
- So Avail file handles hold a RandomAccessFile: its getChannel() FileChannel
  does positional read/write/truncate inside runtime.ioSystem.executeFileTask
  (the suspendThen shape the metadata primitives already use), and its getFD()
  gives FileDescriptor.sync() for P_FileSync.
- RandomAccessFile takes only a mode string ("r", "rw"), so CREATE_NEW,
  APPEND, and creation-time FileAttributes (permissions) need handling before
  the open (e.g. Files.createFile(path, attrs) for create; APPEND as a
  handle-side position).  Map the existing P_FileOpen option set onto that.
- Touches IOSystem.openFile / openFileWithAvailThread, FileHandle, and
  P_FileOpen, P_FileClose, P_FileRead, P_FileWrite, P_FileSync,
  P_FileTruncate, P_FileRefresh.  StacksErrorLog, StacksOutputFile,
  GraphTracer, FileSystemModuleRootResolver also use AsynchronousFileChannel;
  decide whether they move too.
- Option 1 (tests avoid needless writer closes) is still worth doing if the
  fsync cost remains visible; measure first.
Result: with Synchronize_ as plain fsync through a companion descriptor, Mark's 400-run timing of the Avail test suite reached 122 ms (from about 310-400 ms warm).

title: Make the avail test task depend on the Avail module sources
description:
Problem: the avail project's test task does not declare the Avail module sources as inputs, so Gradle treats it as up to date after an Avail-only change and reports the previous run's results. A change that edits or deletes .avail files can show "BUILD SUCCESSFUL" from ./gradlew build without any Avail test having run against it.

Observed: after deleting a library module (Rational Number.avail), ./gradlew build finished in 2 s with the earlier test results; ./gradlew test --rerun was needed to actually run the suite (41 s).

Where: avail/build.gradle.kts, tasks.test. It passes the roots only as systemProperty("availRoots", availRoots) (computed by computeAvailRootsForTest()), and declares no file inputs for them. The build's other tasks show the pattern for declaring inputs (inputs.files(fileTree(...) { include(...) }), inputs.dir(...)).

Fix: declare the source trees of every root the tests load as test inputs: the .avail files under distro/src (the avail, examples, and builder-tests roots, and any others computeAvailRootsForTest() names), with relative path sensitivity. Exclude the compiled module caches (.repo directories) and anything else the tests write, or every run will invalidate the next.

Check: after the fix, editing one .avail file makes ./gradlew build rerun the tests, and an unchanged tree still lets them be up to date.

title: Implement all Avail file operations through FFM instead of NIO
description:
Goal: implement every Avail file operation directly on the operating system's file interface through the JDK's Foreign Function & Memory API (java.lang.foreign), and stop using NIO (FileChannel, AsynchronousFileChannel, Files) for file I/O. This gives Avail precise control over ordering and durability, so it can host something like a database engine.

Why NIO is inadequate:
- On macOS, FileChannel.force (with either metaData flag) issues fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC) (JDK-8080589, JDK 9; JDK-8232861 refined its failure handling). That flushes the drive's entire write cache: about 16-20 ms per flush, shared by the whole drive. While one is in flight, every metadata-changing call on the volume (create, chmod, unlink) waits for it. A standalone benchmark measured create, chmod, and unlink at about 20.8 ms each beside concurrent F_FULLFSYNC, against under 0.1 ms alone. Plain fsync added about 0.01 ms.
- NIO exposes no weaker sync, no write barrier, no O_DSYNC on every path, and no preallocation, and it hides the file descriptor.

Shape:
- Avail's file handles own native descriptors (POSIX int fd; Windows HANDLE). The calls: open, pread, pwrite, ftruncate, the sync family, fcntl, fstat, fchmod/fchown, rename, unlink, mkdir, readdir, realpath, close. They run on the I/O system's file executor, resuming the calling fiber on completion (see avail-6s8 for the suspendable-primitive shape).
- Sync levels, chosen explicitly by Avail code instead of one fixed meaning:
  - ordering: the writes before the barrier reach media before the writes after it (macOS F_BARRIERFSYNC; elsewhere the nearest equivalent, or the next level up).
  - drive: data and the metadata needed to read it back reach the drive (fsync / fdatasync).
  - durable: also survives power loss (macOS F_FULLFSYNC; on Linux fsync already flushes the drive cache; Windows FlushFileBuffers).
- Errors carry errno (or GetLastError), captured with Linker.Option.captureCallState, and map to AvailErrorCodes.

Cross-platform (the largest part of the cost):
- macOS, Linux, and Windows each need their own bindings, constants, and semantics. Struct layouts (stat), constant values (O_*, F_*), and variadic fcntl differ by platform and architecture (x86_64 and arm64). Windows uses a different API (CreateFileW, ReadFile/WriteFile with OVERLAPPED, FlushFileBuffers, SetFileInformationByHandle).
- jextract can generate the bindings from the system headers, per platform, but it is a build-time tool; decide whether to generate or hand-write the comparatively small set needed.
- The tests must run on each supported platform, or at least on those available to CI.

Notes:
- The JVM flag --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED is already required for a usable look and feel. It is set for packageApp (avail/build.gradle.kts) and in the Avail Project Manager run configuration.
- The test and JUnit launches need the flag as well.
- Kotlin–Avail parity: new error codes, changed failure sets, and the sync levels need library bindings, documentation, and Avail tests.
- Supersedes the idea of a second, FFM-opened descriptor held beside each NIO channel just for fsync, and the question of whether closing a file writer should synchronize; settle both here.
notes:
From avail-6s8 (2026-11-10): P_FileRead and P_FileWrite still create a fiber to deliver each result, taking success and failure functions and a priority. Converting them to suspending primitives was deliberately left to this bead, since their NIO paths are replaced here anyway. Every other file primitive already suspends and runs on the I/O system's file executor; follow that shape (suspendThen + runtime.ioSystem.executeFileTask) and remove the library's fiber-returning "a fiber reading…"/"a fiber writing…" file methods, as was done for sync, truncate, rename, and directory creation.
avail-yjt moves Avail file handles to RandomAccessFile and makes
Synchronize_ a plain fsync via FileDescriptor.sync(); F_FULLFSYNC is dropped
(Mark's ruling).  This bead's remaining reasons: the ordering level
(F_BARRIERFSYNC), an optional durable level (document it as a
whole-filesystem flush on macOS), O_DSYNC, preallocation, and leaving NIO.

title: Rework fiber-creating file primitives as suspendable primitives
description:
Description:
- Several file primitives, P_FileSync among them, start their work by creating a new fiber. That fiber runs the success or failure function from the I/O system's callback.
- These primitives may predate parts of the suspendable-primitive mechanism.
- Instead, they should suspend the calling fiber and resume it from the I/O system's completion callback, the way reads and writes do. They would no longer create a fiber just to deliver the result.
- Ruling: don't create a fiber merely to handle a suspendable primitive.

Scope:
1. Make P_FileOpen suspendable, running its work on the I/O system's file executor and resuming the fiber from the completion callback. It currently blocks an interpreter thread for the whole open: about 20 ms while a concurrent F_FULLFSYNC is committing, and the workbench profile showed it averaging 19 ms.
2. Do the same for the other synchronous calls that change metadata: P_FileSetPermissions (about 9 ms) and P_FileUnlink (about 4.6 ms). Others, such as P_FileMetadata and rename, are worth checking.
3. Convert the existing fiber-creating primitives, starting with P_FileSync, which currently does newFiber(...) and then runtime.ioSystem.executeFileTask { force(true) … runOutermostFunction(newFiber, …) }. Audit the remaining file and I/O primitives for the same pattern.

Notes:
- The number of these operations in flight at once becomes bounded by the I/O thread pool's size instead of the interpreter threads. That's acceptable: it frees the interpreter threads.
- Evidence:
  - The workbench's L2Simple statistics: P_FileOpen averaged 19.9 ms, P_FileSetPermissions 9.2 ms, and P_FileUnlink 4.6 ms.
  - A standalone benchmark: create, chmod, and unlink each took about 20.8 ms beside concurrent F_FULLFSYNC, against under 0.1 ms alone.
- Primitives whose failure codes or Avail-side bindings change also need their library methods, tests, and documentation updated (Kotlin–Avail parity).
notes:
Landed (2026-11-10, with avail-7i6):
- Every synchronous file primitive that touches the file system now suspends its fiber and runs on the I/O system's file executor: P_FileOpen; the metadata-changing P_FileUnlink, P_FileMove, P_FileCopy, P_FileSetPermissions, P_FileSetOwner, P_FileSetGroup; the read-only P_FileExists, P_FileCanRead, P_FileCanWrite, P_FileCanExecute, P_FileSize, P_FileGetOwner, P_FileGetGroup, P_FileGetPermissions, P_FileMetadata, P_FileRealPath, P_FilesAreSame; and P_FileClose (which now forgets the handle before closing). Their failure codes are unchanged. Primitives that never touch the disk stay synchronous.
- The fiber-creating P_FileSync, P_FileTruncate, P_FileRename, and P_CreateDirectory now suspend instead, without success/failure/priority arguments. Library: Synchronize_with file system and Truncate_to_bytes⁇with file system replace the fiber-returning methods; Rename_to_ and Create a directory named_ call the primitives directly; the fiber-returning variants are removed.
- The socket primitives (P_SocketRead, P_SocketWrite, P_SocketIPv4Connect, P_SocketIPv6Connect, P_ServerSocketAccept) suspend and are resumed by the JVM's completion handler. The fiber-returning network methods are removed; the synchronous methods moved into Client/Primitives.avail and Server/Primitives.avail, and both Synchronous.avail modules were deleted. The network tests fork their own fibers where they need concurrency.
- Primitive.kt: the L2Simple nilpotent-attempt path (L2SimpleTranslator.attemptToEmbedInvocation) now refuses primitives that can suspend or invoke, matching the normal call path (canRunAtSimpleCallSite).

Correction to the description: P_FileRead and P_FileWrite also create fibers; they do not show the suspending shape. Ruling (Mark): their conversion belongs to avail-rlc, where reads and writes are rebuilt on FFM.

Out of scope by ruling: P_ExecuteAttachedExternalProcess creates a fiber attached to the child process's standard streams, which is its purpose, like a fork.

title: Benchmark tracking: catch performance regressions, then guide L2 and translation work
description:
Set up benchmarks whose results are recorded and compared over time.  The
first goal is to catch unnecessary slowdowns of 2x or so before they land.
The second is to measure, and so drive, improvements in L2 execution
speed.  Later, the same setup measures the cost of L2 translation and
optimization itself.

What exists today:
- avail.performance: Statistic, PerInterpreterStatistic, and the
  StatisticReport categories (FINAL_JVM_TRANSLATION_TIME, PRIMITIVES,
  REIFICATIONS, dynamic lookups, type checks, (de)serialization,
  ALLOCATIONS_BY_DESCRIPTOR_CLASS, ...).  These give per-run profiles inside
  the VM, but nothing records them or compares them between runs.
- "Time all tests_times" in Avail Tests.avail prints the wall time of each
  full test pass.  It's crude, but it covers the whole system.
- There is no JMH or kotlinx-benchmark in the build.

Ways to measure:
1. JMH, through the kotlinx-benchmark Gradle plugin or the me.champeau.jmh
   plugin.  This is the standard JVM harness: it handles warm-up, forks,
   statistics, and blackholes, and has profilers for allocation (gc) and
   JIT behavior.  It suits Kotlin-level microbenchmarks such as dispatch,
   type checks, tuple operations, and L2 translation of fixed functions.
   Adding it needs Mark's approval.
2. Benchmarks written in Avail, run by a small Kotlin or JMH harness that
   loads modules once and then times entry points: Avail workloads that run
   through L1, L2, and the JVM-translated chunks.  These are the most
   relevant to L2 work.
3. Counts that don't depend on timing: L2 instructions executed, chunks
   translated, reifications, deoptimizations, and allocations.  These are
   repeatable from run to run, so a change in one is a precise signal even
   on a noisy machine, and the existing Statistic machinery can collect
   them.  A 2x slowdown nearly always shows up as a jump in some count.
4. Compile-time measures: translation and optimization time per function,
   from FINAL_JVM_TRANSLATION_TIME and similar statistics, together with
   the size of each chunk's output (L2 instructions and JVM bytecode).

Ways to track:
- Write each run's results as JSON, keyed by commit, and compare them with
  a saved baseline.  Fail, or warn, when a ratio crosses a threshold such
  as 1.5x for times, or any change at all for counts.  This can be a Gradle
  task, which needs no external service.
- Hosted options exist: Bencher, github-action-benchmark with its GitHub
  Pages charts, and Conbench.  They're optional; local JSON plus a report is
  enough to start, and keeps the data in-house.
- Noise: a 2x threshold tolerates ordinary laptop noise.  Finer goals need
  the same machine, a quiet system, several JMH forks, and medians.

First steps to propose and break down: choose the harness (JMH via a
plugin, or a custom harness); define a small first suite (one or two
fixed-workload Avail entry points plus a few microbenchmarks); add the
deterministic counts; choose the result format and comparison tool.

title: Fix Dokka: kotlinx-html resolution failure in dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml
description:
./gradlew dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml fails in avail (and in
avail-artifact, which it includes) during dependency resolution of the
Dokka HTML generator's runtime classpath:

  Could not resolve all dependencies for configuration
  ':dokkaHtmlGeneratorRuntimeResolver~internal'.
  Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Edge
  org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-html-jvm:0.9.1 (jvmRuntimeElements-published)
  -> org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib-common:1.8.20 has no target nodes.

Gradle surfaces it as "Problems writing to Binary store in
~/.gradle/.tmp/gradle*.bin", and with the configuration cache on, as a
cache serialization error; --no-configuration-cache shows the same root
cause.  It is the same error that kept gradle-plugin on Dokka 2.1.0 during
the Gradle 9.8.2 / Kotlin 2.4.21 upgrade (commit 8a4d05e18), which likely
introduced it.  Suspects: kotlin-stdlib-common no longer being published
for Kotlin 2.4 (no matching variant), a dependency-resolution or
substitution rule in the build, or a Dokka version mismatch with Gradle 9.8.

Dokka is the KDoc link checker named in CLAUDE.md's "Verifying a Change",
so until it is fixed new KDoc links go unchecked.  Done when
dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml succeeds in avail (and gradle-plugin can move
to the same Dokka version), with the configuration cache on.
notes:
Symptom as of 2026-11-10 (after the Gradle 9.8.2 / Kotlin 2.4.21 upgrade),
running ./gradlew dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml from avail/, inside or outside
the sandbox:  configuration cache could not be cached: field
__runtimeClasspath__ of task :avail-artifact:dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml ...
Could not resolve all dependencies for configuration
':avail-artifact:dokkaHtmlGeneratorRuntimeResolver~internal' > Problems
writing to Binary store in ~/.gradle/.tmp/gradle<N>.bin (exist: true).
Fails in about 1 s, before any KDoc is processed.  Disk space is fine.
Try first: --no-configuration-cache to separate the cache serialization
from the resolution failure, then --stacktrace on the resolution.
Root cause (2026-11-10): not Gradle 9.8 (Gradle 9.6.0 and 9.8.0 fail too) and
not the Kotlin 2.4 stdlib-common metadata (unchanged in shape since 2.0).
Dokka 2.3.0's modules require kotlin-stdlib 2.1.21 (2.1.0 required only
2.0.21).  ~/.m2 holds kotlin-stdlib 2.1.21 as a Maven download: POM + jar,
no Gradle .module, though the POM carries the published-with-gradle-metadata
marker.  Every Avail build lists mavenLocal() before mavenCentral(), so Gradle
takes that POM-only stdlib, mixes it with metadata-published
kotlin-stdlib-common, and trips an internal error: "Edge kotlinx-html-jvm:0.9.1
-> kotlin-stdlib-common:1.8.20 has no target nodes", surfaced as "Problems
writing to Binary store".
Minimal repro (scratchpad repro2): kotlin("jvm") 2.4.21 + Dokka 2.3.0, one
class.  Passes with mavenCentral() only; fails when mavenLocal() is added;
passes again with mavenLocal { content { includeGroup("org.availlang") } }.

title: Navigate from IntelliJ stack frames to dumped L2 classes and .l2 files
description:
When debugging a live VM in IntelliJ, stack frames in generated JVMChunk
classes cannot be navigated: neither to the dumped .class file nor, ideally,
to the .l2 text, whose line numbers the class's LineNumberTable already
records.  Making this work would let a JVM debugger step through L2 code.

What exists (optimizer/jvm/JVMTranslator.kt, with debugJVM enabled):
- Each chunk's .class is dumped under debug/jvm/<package path>/ (relative
  to the process working directory, so avail/debug/jvm when run from
  avail/), beside its .l1, .l2, .dot, and .simple.dot files.
- The class records SourceFile as the .l2 file name, e.g. "0000
  group_by_#1.l2", and its line numbers refer to lines of that .l2 file.
- Class names are derived from module and method names, e.g.
  avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.Maps.0000_group_by_#1 (2).group_by_#1.
  The package segments contain spaces, parentheses, '#', and characters
  such as '«', which are not Java identifiers.

Likely causes to investigate:
- The debugger resolves a frame's source as <package dirs>/<SourceFile>
  under a source root; debug/jvm is not a source root, and the .l2 file
  is not where that lookup would place it, or IntelliJ cannot map the
  non-identifier package names to directories at all.
- The class files are not on any classpath IntelliJ knows about.

Possible directions: sanitize generated package and class names to valid
identifiers (keeping a readable mapping), lay out the dump so that
<package dirs>/<SourceFile> names the .l2 file exactly, and register
debug/jvm as a source root (or document how to attach it) so the .l2 file
opens at the frame's line.
notes:
Findings (2026-11-06, verified by Mark in IntelliJ):
- Generated classes now use Java-identifier names:
  avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.<Module>.L<line>_<function>_v<n>.<function>,
  dumped under avail/debug/jvm mirroring the package
  (JVMTranslator.prepareOutputDirectory).
- IntelliJ's Java debugger finds a frame's source by looking up a Java file
  that declares the class, through its index, within the run configuration's
  module scope.  A plain .l2 file declares nothing, so it is never found.
  Hence JVMTranslator.dumpL2ListingAsJava = true: the listing is written as
  <function>.java, declaring the class, with the listing in a comment on
  unchanged lines.
- avail/.idea/misc.xml had the project compiler output set to
  $PROJECT_DIR$/debug/jvm, and IntelliJ never indexes the project output
  directory.  Changed to $PROJECT_DIR$/out (misc.xml is untracked).
- IntelliJ setup that works: avail/debug/jvm as a content root of module
  avail.main, marked Sources, and listed under Settings > Compiler >
  Excludes (the project builds with IntelliJ's own compiler,
  delegatedBuild = false, so the stubs must not be compiled).  A Gradle
  re-sync may drop the content root.
- Register names (r0, i1, ...) come from the class's LocalVariableTable,
  now emitted whenever debugJVM is on; locals are not initialized, so a
  register not yet written shows no meaningful value.
Remaining option if the .java form is unwanted: an IntelliJ plugin with a
PositionManagerFactory mapping avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.* frames to
debug/jvm/<sourcePath>, which would make plain .l2 work.
Preferred solution (Mark, 2026-11-06): Kotlin listings with the original
class names.  JVMTranslator.l2ListingFormat = L2ListingFormat.KOTLIN and
useOriginalClassNames = true.  Each generated class lives in package
avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.<module>.<line>_<function> (<n>) and its
listing is <function>.kt, declaring the class with every name segment in
backticks and the listing inside a block comment (both /* and */ broken
apart, since Kotlin comments nest).  Verified in IntelliJ: double-clicking
a generated frame opens the .kt listing at the right L2 instruction, and
register locals (r0, i1, ...) show by name.  kotlinc 2.4.21 compiles these
listings to classes with exactly the generated names; '%' only draws a
Windows warning.

The JAVA format (with Java-identifier names, useOriginalClassNames = false)
and the plain TEXT format (.l2, not navigable) remain selectable.

IntelliJ setup that navigation needs: debug/jvm is a content root of module
avail.main marked Sources, listed under Compiler > Excludes, and the project
output (misc.xml) is NOT debug/jvm (it was, which stopped indexing).

title: L2 function inlining
description:
Inline called functions into the caller's L2 control flow graph.

Context for breaking it down: Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 9.2 notes
that L2ValueManifest.transform (currently without callers) is intended for
inlining called graphs, where the callee's stack slots must be distinguished
from the caller's via Frame, and that post-phi data keyed by semantic values
must be transformed along with it.  Survey what inlining the optimizer already
does before proposing children.
notes:
Mark's account of L2ValueManifest.transform (2026-11-11): it maps a Frame
instance, used as a namespace inside L2SemanticSlot and other semantic
values, into a Frame representing one particular invocation within a parent
Frame.  The namespaces stay separate except at call, return, reification and
reentry sites, so that an L2 graph of a called function (probably captured
before the last few optimization passes) can be embedded into a caller's
CFG.  The design doc cited above was rewritten as
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Post_phi_data.md and no longer discusses
transform; post-phi data (PostPhiData, keyed by L2Synonym of semantic values)
must be mapped through the same transform when a callee graph is embedded.
Related: avail-zv7 (Uniform variables and freeze hook for full inlining) records the design discussion of 2026-11-16/17 on what inlining needs from variables and reification: postponed Creates as the escape point, a freeze hook on L2_RETURN_FROM_REIFICATION_HANDLER that turns an L2-friendly continuation (possibly standing for several inlined frames) into L1-friendly ones, loop versioning for variables live around loops, safety versioning at polymorphic call sites, and inlining triggers (fresh closure arguments, continuations, known flow-control primitives).  Read its notes before proposing children here.
Inlining guidance (2026-11-17): prioritize closures that capture a label or are passed one; label creation makes the whole call stack immutable (materializing elided variables), so inlining it saves both the jump and that freeze.  See avail-zv7.2 (labels and backtracking via fiber variables) and avail-zv7.3 (exception handling via catcher entry points).

title: Remove what post-phi data makes unnecessary; add the never-used exclusion pass
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 8 lists mechanisms the post-phi data makes
unnecessary, and a never-used exclusion pass it makes possible.  Remove the
former and add the latter, once the invariants of the sibling beads are
asserted.
notes:
The old design doc's section 8, preserved here since the doc was rewritten as
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Post_phi_data.md (which describes only what
exists).  Note: L2_MOVE's BySemanticValue regeneration also leaves an L2_NOP
("transformed move") when it folds a move into a same-block definition.

## 8. What this makes unnecessary, and what it improves

- **Explicit edge transport, and any need for input/output edge
  correspondence.** Rewrites that change the shape of control flow are then
  free: a multi-way tag branch becoming one-direction jumps, `≤` rewritten as
  `>` or `=` according to the boundaries of known restrictions, elision of
  edges all of whose paths lead to impossible conditions, and jump elision to
  enlarge basic blocks.
- **The `L2_NOP` tombstone** that `removeDeadInstructions` leaves where it drops
  an instruction. It is a witness with its content thrown away.
- Probably **the base fabrication in `recordDerivation`**. It exists because a
  derived value can be bound while its base is unknown; if the base's synonymy
  is transported, the base should already be present. The restriction seeded
  from the tag (commit `a3cf993db`) is a narrower patch for the same hole and
  may become redundant.
- **Dead code elimination gets stronger, not weaker.** Previously the only
  record that `x` and `z` were synonymous might be two overlapping facts,
  `[x,y]` and `[y,z]`, so `y` could not be dropped without losing the
  relationship. A `postPhiData` records the synonym `{x,y,z}` directly, so
  `y` can be dropped outright. Once semantic values and registers that are
  never used or populated have been identified, they can be excluded from every
  manifest in a fresh regeneration pass, and synonyms left empty are dropped.
Unblocked (2026-11-14).  Its sibling invariants turned out to be unnecessary: avail-ezf.1, avail-ezf.3, and avail-ezf.5 were closed as obsolete (see their closing notes), and avail-ezf.2's monotonicity checks landed in commit 5facba4e2.  So 'once the invariants of the sibling beads are asserted' is satisfied.  The never-used exclusion pass must not assume every post-phi value has a producer: a known value with no producer is harmless and worth keeping as knowledge.  Reproduce failures with L2Optimizer.shouldSanityCheck set true locally.  Its notes still have the old section 8's garbled bold markup ('input/output**** edge ****correspondence', '**The **L2_NOP** tombstone**').
Resolved (2026-11-14) per Mark: edge transport dropped (never built; the rewrites it would enable are separate optimizations); the L2_NOP diagnostics stay; the anchor introduced by recordInvocationUse stays, its congruence already covered by L2ValueManifestTest; the never-used exclusion pass is set aside, apart from the test invocationKeepsItsArgumentKnown.
close_reason: Done: items resolved per Mark; added invocationKeepsItsArgumentKnown

title: Postpone, rather than drop, inputs read only by postponed instructions
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 5 (closing note) and 10.4: an input that
is read only by a postponed instruction must itself be postponed rather than
dropped.  Check whether this holds today; fix it if not.  The failure it
causes resembles the ones the post-phi design exists to end.
notes:
The old doc's section 5 closing note, preserved here since the doc was
rewritten as avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Post_phi_data.md: a postponed
instruction's reads are not uses of its inputs.  Dead code elimination walks
the instruction graph, and a postponed instruction is not in it, so an input
read only by a postponement looks unused.  It may be postponed in turn, but
it must not be dropped, or the postponement becomes unemittable.
Ground changed by avail-ezf.2 (commit 5facba4e2):
- Postponed moves are no longer recorded.  L2_GET_UNESCAPED_LOCAL_VARIABLE and L2_GET_AND_CLEAR_IF_MUTABLE_UNESCAPED_LOCAL_VARIABLE now agglomerate synonyms instead, so a move is never the postponed instruction whose input could be dropped.
- To reproduce optimizer failures, set L2Optimizer.shouldSanityCheck = true locally (never commit it as true).  It now also checks that regenerated edges and single-input blocks do not weaken (L2ValueManifest.isStrongerThanManifest), and a dropped input should surface there or in checkEdgesAndPhis.  With it on, the full build passed at 5facba4e2.
- A jump-only block is now kept when its post-phi data is the only record of a fact (Post_phi_data.md §Jump-only blocks).
Obsolete (2026-11-13).  The hazard cannot arise:
- Liveness and dead-code removal are computed only on complete graphs, scanning backward from returns, reification-handler returns, and loop back edges.  During the postponement pass, dead-code decisions come from the old graph, where the would-be-postponed instruction is an ordinary reader of its inputs, so their writers survive whenever it does.
- Regeneration never drops a semantic value because liveness says it is dead.  Values are dropped only at L2_JUMP_BACK (clearPostponedInstructions, after the kept reads force emission), at L2_STRIP_MANIFEST (whose input reads force emission), and on L2_SAVE_ALL_AND_PC_TO_INT's backward reference edge (clearPostponedInstructions).  No postponed instruction outlives one of its inputs.
- At a merge, a postponed instruction carried on every incoming edge has its inputs known on every edge too, so they merge with it.
close_reason: Obsolete: liveness runs only on complete graphs, and every point that drops values first clears or forces postponed instructions

title: Assert each output edge is at least as informative as its input edge
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md sections 6 and 10.3: after regeneration and
post-phi replay, each output edge's manifest must be at least as informative
as the corresponding input edge's (the monotonicity law).  Add a per-edge
assertion.  Verify against testSemanticRestrictionOfSetCreation_1.
notes:
The design doc is now avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Post_phi_data.md; the
law is §Monotonicity, replay is §Replay.  Found while rewriting it: when
regeneration writes a value the replayed data already knows,
L2ValueManifest.recordDefinitionNoCheck (existing-semantic-value branch)
*replaces* the synonym's restriction with the writer's rather than
intersecting it, so a write whose restriction is wider than the replayed one
weakens the manifest.  Expect this assertion to fire there first; decide
whether the writer's restriction should be intersected (the comment says the
replacement is deliberate for reuse of colored registers, so check that case).
testSemanticRestrictionOfSetCreation_1 is still in SimpleOptimizerTest.
Correction to the note above: recordDefinitionNoCheck does not weaken the restriction.  Its lambda answers the writer's restriction, but updateRestriction always intersects the lambda's answer with the old restriction (L2ValueManifest.updateRestriction).  The misleading 'Replace the restriction entirely' comment was corrected in the avail-3oj.2 commit.  The assertion is still worth adding; there is no known violation to expect first.
Cold-start notes (2026-11-12, after commits 1c49c28b3, c780e0cec, a5ed2cdb7):
- "Section 6 and 10.3" in the description refer to the deleted
  Declared_Manifest_Effects.md; the law is Post_phi_data.md §Monotonicity.
  The manifest itself is now described in
  doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Value_manifest.md - read §Merging and
  §Narrowing first: merges now propagate a narrower merged restriction and
  merge congruent invocations (mergeValueClasses), which makes output edges
  more informative than before, not less.
- "At least as informative" needs a comparison over two manifests from
  different graphs, so it must be phrased in terms of semantic values, not
  ValueClass ids or registers (both are per manifest/graph): for each
  synonym of the input edge's post-phi-relevant facts, the output edge
  must hold its members in one class with a restriction at least as strong
  (TypeRestriction.isStrongerThan).  Phi generation is the one sanctioned
  weakening (§Monotonicity), and edges into a specialized (split) block
  only strengthen.  Decide which edges correspond: L2Regenerator maps old
  blocks to new ones in processSourceGraph.
- Gate the check like check(): behind deepManifestDebugCheck, since it is
  costly.

title: Assert the witness invariant on each post-phi capture
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 5: every synonym captured in post-phi
data must have a witness, namely a register holding it, a constant
restriction, or a self-describing member.  Assert this at capture time.  It is
the property the design turns on, and it would catch a value whose only
witness was a postponement.
notes:
The design doc was renamed and rewritten as
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Post_phi_data.md (spec post-phi-data).  The
witness discussion was moved out of it into avail-ezf.5 (its design field
holds the old section 5 text), because it is not yet certain that every
witness kind survives without the manifest's postponed information.  This bead
now depends on avail-ezf.5: assert whatever invariant that investigation
establishes.
Obsolete (2026-11-14).  Asserting a witness for every synonym captured in post-phi data would reject facts worth keeping: a known value with no producer is harmless, since nothing reads it (see avail-ezf.5's closing note).  What matters is that anything turning knowledge into a read asks whether the value can be produced, not whether it is known, and the populated-register check in checkEdgesAndPhis already catches a read of a value that cannot be produced.
close_reason: Obsolete: a known value without a producer is harmless; reads must ask producibility, not knownness

title: Make avail/doc/Optimization normative
description:
Bring every document under avail/doc/Optimization in line with the rule that
design docs are normative: they describe the system as it is, in the present
tense, with no plan, status line, step sequence, dates, or session log.  The
plan lives in bd.  These docs are also what wovenspec (avail-docs) will serve,
so what they say must be true of the code.

title: Hoist loop-body type tests by unrolling one iteration
description: Use the result of an earlier loop generation pass to decide whether to build a variation without an inner type test that always holds (or never holds), hoisting the test out of the loop by unrolling one iteration.

title: Int-register conditions at loop heads
description: Specialize loop variations that keep values in int registers across the loop.

title: Drop duplicate loop variations
description: Compare a newly generated loop variation's instructions with earlier ones, and reuse a match instead of keeping a copy.

title: Generate loop-head variations and link backward branches
description: Build a loop head and body specialized for a set of conditions, and connect each backward branch to the most specific variation that satisfies it.

title: Propagate split conditions backward to loop heads
description: Carry the L2SplitConditions requested inside a loop body back along its backward branches to the loop head, so the head can be split on them.

title: Loop splitting
description:
Extend L2 code splitting to loop heads.  A loop head is split into
variations specialized for the L2SplitConditions propagated backward to it
(see avail/src/main/kotlin/avail/optimizer/L2SplitCondition.kt), and each
backward branch that closes a loop connects to the most specific available
variation of the loop head.

When a backward branch from a generated body requests conditions that no
existing variation satisfies, generate a new variation, then compare its
instructions against the previously generated variations; if it is
equivalent to one of them, reuse that one and discard the duplicate.

Kinds of condition:
- A value must be in an int register.
- A type condition tested inside the body holds (or never holds).

For a type test inside the body, use the result of a previous loop
generation pass to decide whether to create a variation without the test.
Doing so hoists the test out of the loop by unrolling one iteration.
notes: Related: avail-zv7's notes describe loop versioning for variables still elided on reaching a loop: generate a first version assuming they stay postponed, jump back to it if they do, otherwise create a new version with the variables created so far passed to its top.  That is a loop-splitting variant keyed on which variables are still postponed.

title: Explore exception handling via catcher entry points
description:
Explore exception handling under inlining, using the alternate-entry-point pattern of the freeze subgraph.

Inlining a P_CatchException call could produce a catcher entry point in the chunk, much like the freeze subgraph on L2_RETURN_FROM_REIFICATION_HANDLER.  During P_RaiseException, after reifying the stack, the runtime would invoke that entry point for each frame's chunk to determine whether the frame wants to catch the exception or run a finally block, instead of walking frames for handler markers.

Stack traces: if only a summary of the stack trace is needed, it can be collected frame by frame as the walk exits frames this way.  The stack would not have to be made immutable unless the full trace is actually used at the catch site; at that point a reification could collect the remainder of the stack.

Caution (from avail-zv7's notes): an embedded P_CatchException frame inside a fused, inlined frame is tricky to get right; handler markers must still be found, and a single L2 continuation may stand for several L1 frames.

Work: explore and write up the design (as a section of the avail-zv7.1 design doc or its own doc), covering how a raise finds and invokes catcher entry points, finally blocks, the lazy stack-trace collection, and interaction with multi-frame expansion; then file implementation beads.

title: Document inlining of labels and backtracking via fiber variables
description:
Document how inlining can make label-based control flow and backtracking as fast as loops.

Label creation reifies the stack and makes the entire call stack immutable, so that the caller and the label's caller can refer to the same continuation; that materializes every elided variable in those frames (at least the upper frames not already made immutable by an earlier label).  Guiding inlining along closures that capture a label, or are passed one, therefore pays twice: the looping or early exit itself becomes a jump, and the call chain no longer has to be made immutable.

Backtracking in Avail stores its state in fiber variables.  Once an optimization short-circuits P_LookupFiberVariable after a P_SetFiberVariable of the same key (the lookup answers the value just set, with nothing in between that could change it), inlined backtracking code can in principle run as fast as a loop.

Work: write this up as part of the inlining / uniform-variables design (avail-zv7.1, or the inlining epic avail-6zs), including the conditions under which the set/lookup short-circuit is valid (no intervening set of the same key, no fiber switch or call that could observe or change the fiber's variables), and file implementation beads from it.  Example to study: the Backtracking module's first try (debug dump Backtracking/0246_first_try#1, blocks ~9-14, where the caller is made immutable for backtracking).

title: Find a faster alternative to the 3.5-minute Dokka run
description:
Running `./gradlew dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml` takes about 3.5 minutes every time, even when little has changed, which makes the KDoc-link check (part of verifying every changeset) expensive.

Investigate faster ways to get the same guarantee, that every KDoc link resolves and docs render:
- Dokka configuration: incremental or cached generation, Gradle build cache / configuration cache, restricting source sets or suppressing unneeded outputs, running with a larger heap, the newer Dokka Gradle plugin modes.
- A lighter link-check-only path (for example a Dokka task without HTML rendering, or another KDoc analyzer) for routine verification, keeping the full HTML build for publishing.
- Alternative documentation generators for Kotlin, if any resolve KDoc links with comparable fidelity.

Measure each option against the current baseline on this repository, and recommend one.

title: Postpone into all branches, then lift instructions common to every arm (and out of loops)
description:
Postpone instructions into every branch, then lift back what runs on all of them.

Today a postponed instruction travels down every outgoing edge of a branch, and is emitted once per path that reads it.  Nothing recovers the case where every path reads it: the computation stays duplicated below the branch.  (The old "always live along every successor edge" check in basicRegenerateForPostponement tested the instruction's own target edges, so it never fired, and was removed.)

Direction (Mark's ruling):

- Always allow postponement into multiple branches.
- Add a pass that repeatedly moves back above a branch any instruction that is present along all of its arms and depends on no instruction after the branch point.  Repeating it lifts everything that runs unconditionally back to before the branch, while instructions stay diverged when they depend on different predecessors (for example, in a code-split path where an input to a duplicated instruction is a constant on one arm but not on another).
- The same lifting generalizes to loops: hoisting computations and tests out of loops, lifting before loop heads / jump-backs as well as branches.

Intended overall shape of the pipeline:

1. Generate.
2. Regular code splitting.
3. Find loop split conditions; duplicate loop versions.
4. Find more loop split conditions (enabled by the previous loop splits, if any); generate any new useful loop versions.
5. Eliminate dead code.
6. Lift instructions before branches *or* loop heads / jump-backs.
7. Never regenerate BySemanticValue again afterward, since postponement would "unlift" the lifting work.

Interactions to keep in mind:

- Placeholders (L2_VIRTUAL_CREATE_LABEL) must stay mobile until REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER_INSTRUCTIONS; lifting must not undo their late placement, or must run after replacement.
- Identity of "the same instruction on every arm" must be semantic (same operation, same semantic inputs), not register-based, since each arm was regenerated separately.

title: Read the latest return value only at entry points; remove LATEST_RETURN_VALUE
description:
Read the latest return value only at entry points, then remove the LATEST_RETURN_VALUE hidden variable.

Today L2_GET_LATEST_RETURN_VALUE is the only reader of Interpreter's latest result, used in two places:
- At the reentry point after a reified call (CallSiteHelper, the ReificationWithCheck and ReificationNoCheck exits), capturing the value being returned into the on-ramp.
- In a primitive's failure path at function start (L1Translator, after L2_TRY_PRIMITIVE fails), capturing the failure code into the first local constant.

Mark's idea: fold the first read into a variant of L2_ENTER_L2_CHUNK.  An entry point can be neither postponed nor moved, so it would be the only thing reading the latest return value, and the hidden variable, with its interference bookkeeping, could go away.  The failure-code read is not at an entry point, so it needs its own answer, most likely having L2_TRY_PRIMITIVE write the failure code into a register operand on its failure edge.
design:
Ground as of 2026-11-14:
- Infallible primitives no longer write the latest result: Primitive.generateJvmCodeWithoutTracking calls attemptN and stores the returned value straight into the result register.  LATEST_RETURN_VALUE was therefore taken out of the write interference mask of side-effectless primitives (Primitive.l2WriteInterferenceMask's final branch), which lets their L2_RUN_INFALLIBLE_PRIMITIVE be postponed.
- Declarers of LATEST_RETURN_VALUE: L2_GET_LATEST_RETURN_VALUE (reads), L2_TRY_PRIMITIVE, L2_INVOKE, L2_INVOKE_CONSTANT_FUNCTION (write), and the side-effecting branches of Primitive.l2WriteInterferenceMask.
- Check the JVM translation of each entry point and of L2_TRY_PRIMITIVE's failure edge, and run the stress test (tiny OptimizationLevel countdowns, sanity and deep manifest checks on) after the change.

title: Produce labels on demand as a pseudo-primitive, replacing the placeholder pass
description:
Rewrite L2_VIRTUAL_CREATE_LABEL as a pseudo-primitive invocation, produced on demand by generating its subgraph, and drop the REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER_INSTRUCTIONS pass if every placeholder can be handled the same way.

Today L2_VIRTUAL_CREATE_LABEL is a placeholder (isPlaceholder), replaced by L2Optimizer.replacePlaceholderInstructions with the code that reifies the caller if necessary and creates the label continuation.  L2_MULTIWAY_JUMP is the only other placeholder.

The idea: treat the label as a value whose production is described by its semantic value, like Tag(x) and Variant(x).  An invocation of a pseudo-primitive (with CanFold, assumed infallible and stable like any semantic primitive invocation) names the label; its postponement is elided (canBeElidedFromPostponement), and only when something reads the label does the generator produce it, emitting the label-creation subgraph at that point.  The pseudo-primitive's arguments must first be grouped into a tuple, so the invocation reads a fixed number of values; the tuple operations evaporate once the subgraph reads the elements directly.
design:
Prerequisites:
- Producing a primitive invocation on demand (the production side of avail-gtb): when a synonym has no register, postponed instruction, or constant, the generator builds the value from its invocation.  Today that falls through to L2Generator.constantToProduce, which fails with "cannot produce ...".
- Primitive postponement must actually happen.  As of 2026-11-14 every primitive's l2WriteInterferenceMask includes LATEST_RETURN_VALUE, so Primitive.canBePostponed's default never answers true.

Why it looks tractable: L2Generator.addToCurrentBlock calls aboutToAdd, which produces the instruction's inputs (populateForRead), and only then reads currentBlock to add the instruction.  So producing an input can build a subgraph and leave generation in a continuation block, and the instruction lands there with that block's manifest.  In the regenerator, L2Regenerator.processBlock already replays the old block's post-phi data when an instruction leaves generation in a new block.

Questions to settle:
- Does postponement give a postponed pseudo-primitive the same motility as a placeholder, through the interactions between passes?  A placeholder survives code splitting, postponement, and dead code removal untouched until REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER_INSTRUCTIONS; an elided invocation is instead produced wherever it is first read, in whichever pass reads it.
- Can L2_MULTIWAY_JUMP be handled the same way (it is control flow, not a value), or does it keep the pass alive?
- Where should the label subgraph be produced so that reification sees the right frame state?
notes:
Prerequisites met by avail-gtb (commit 1850884a6, 2026-11-15): side-effectless primitives are postponable again; L2ValueManifest.isProducible / producibleInvocationFor find a runnable invocation in a value's class; L2Generator.ensureDefinedOrEmitMoveBoxed emits an L2_RUN_INFALLIBLE_PRIMITIVE for it via the new raw-function-free constructor L2_RUN_INFALLIBLE_PRIMITIVE(Foldable, arguments, result).  Production today emits a single instruction; generating a subgraph at that point is the new part.  A pseudo-primitive must implement Foldable (the CanFold flag is derived from it; see FoldableTest).  Invocations are assumed infallible and stable wherever known (Value_manifest.md §Semantic values).  Consider settling avail-9dm first, since the motility question depends on what the postponement phases do.
2026-11-20 (after 91475a30f): Primitive.guaranteedType is now the only way to ask a primitive for its guaranteed result type.  An override of returnTypeGuaranteedByVM must carry context(_: GuaranteeContext), which only guaranteedType can supply.  A Foldable pseudo-primitive whose argument types are all enumerations (not metatypes, at most 256 combinations) is folded over the product during type computation through Primitive.foldedResultOrNull, so the label pseudo-primitive must either not be Foldable in that sense or be safe to run that way; folding requires an Interpreter on the current thread.
2026-11-20 design (agreed in discussion): the caller is primary.  L2SemanticCaller(frame) is produced on demand: in a reification zone by L2_GET_CURRENT_CONTINUATION, elsewhere by the reify subgraph from L2_VIRTUAL_CREATE_LABEL.generateReplacement (with its dynamic already-reified check).  The label is the invocation CreateLabel(caller, function, CreateTuple(arguments)) of a Foldable pseudo-primitive, which retires L2SemanticLabel.  Because the caller is never a translation-time constant, constant folding cannot touch the invocation.  Restart and exit recognize a label by the caller in its synonym's invocation, without producing anything.  Plain restart can take its arguments from the invocation.  Fix L2SemanticCaller's KDoc: it is the parent frame at the call site, not the parent's label.  Find how to keep a pseudo-primitive out of the Avail-visible primitive table and generateAllNames.  avail-iel (label/continuation split) later shrinks label production to caller plus one allocation.
2026-11-20 (5b92b20bc): labels no longer capture arguments.  The label invocation is CreateLabel(caller, function), with no CreateTuple(arguments), which supersedes the 2026-11-20 design note on that point.  L2_VIRTUAL_CREATE_LABEL already has no arguments operand and fills every slot with nil.  P_RestartContinuation and L2_RESTART_CONTINUATION are gone; restart and exit recognition now concerns only P_RestartContinuationWithArguments(If) and the two exit primitives, and plain restart no longer reads the frame's argument slots.

title: Separate the type test from checked variable writes
description:
A checked variable write (L2_SET_VARIABLE) performs the type test against
the variable's write type inside the write itself.  The optimizer cannot see
or improve that test.  Split it out: emit an explicit type test of the value
against the variable's write type (an L2 type-test branch such as
L2_JUMP_IF_KIND_OF_OBJECT, with the failure path doing what the failed write
does today), followed by L2_SET_VARIABLE_NO_CHECK on the passing edge.

Why: the separated test can then use the optimizer's specialized type
testing, which tests only what the value's known restriction leaves
uncertain, and code splitting can narrow along the passing and failing
edges.

Example: "untwisted Mersenne Twister from_" in
distro/src/avail/Avail.avail/Data Abstractions.avail/Pseudorandom Number
Generation.avail/Mersenne Twister.avail builds a 624-element tuple with
repeated "vector += ...".  The appended elements are definitely u32, so
the elements already conform, and only the tuple's size should need
testing.  The fused check in the write tests the whole tuple type instead.

Emission sites today:
- L1Translator (around line 2437): the naive local-variable set emits
  L2_SET_VARIABLE when the stored value isn't known to conform.
- P_SetValue (around line 129): emits L2_SET_VARIABLE when the value's
  type is not a subtype of the variable's write type, and
  L2_SET_VARIABLE_NO_CHECK otherwise.

Things to check: the failure semantics of L2_SET_VARIABLE (a type failure
versus a write-reactor/observe failure share its failure edge), so the
separated type test's failure path must produce the same observable
behavior; and whether L2_SET_VARIABLE is still needed afterwards.

title: Find redundant parts of the manifest's equivalence search
description:
Audit L2ValueManifest's equivalence search (equivalentSemanticValue,
equivalentPopulatedSemanticValue, classRestrictingSearchFor,
isEquivalentSemanticValue) for parts that are now purely redundant.

Since the search was written, several things changed how a value is named:
- Semantic constants are canonical per constant (constant(...)), and a
  restriction that becomes a constant joins the constant's synonym.
- Tags and variant ids are ordinary L2SemanticPrimitiveInvocations, and
  congruence (mergeCongruentUsers) merges invocations whose arguments merge.
- Witness kinds are handled separately (see the witness bead split from
  avail-3oj.6).

Question: given those, which branches of the class-filtered linear scan can
ever find something the direct classOf lookup would not?  Candidates: the
constant case (constants are found by key), and primitive invocations whose
arguments are themselves synonyms (congruence should already have merged
them, once usingClasses is maintained correctly - see avail-d33).  Remove
what is provably redundant, keep an assertion-mode cross-check while
proving it, and update the equivalence-search section of the value
manifest design doc.

title: Verify or explain the placeholder TODO and the every-slot replacement in createElidedVariables
description:
Two comments in the variable-elision runtime that Mark should verify or explain, so the design doc and KDoc can state the reason rather than a hedge:

- VariablePlaceholderDescriptor: "TODO: Make this be [Frame]-relative somehow.  Might not be necessary, since it has a usable identity."  Is frame-relativity needed, e.g. for recursion, where two frames of the same chunk hold placeholders for the same local index?
- ContinuationDescriptor.createElidedVariables: "2026.02.28 This seems a bit wonky..." explaining why placeholders are replaced in every frame slot, not only the local slots (a pushed local variable is a synonym of the local's slot, so a reified continuation can hold the placeholder in stack slots too).  Confirm that is the intended design, so the comment can say so plainly.
notes:
Since b7aadbfb1 (avail-9dm): a pushed local is aliased and never elided, so a reified continuation can no longer hold a placeholder in a stack slot; the every-slot replacement in createElidedVariables covers a case that no longer arises.  avail-zv7 removes VariablePlaceholderDescriptor and createElidedVariables altogether, which would make this moot.
Update (d94c7fbb6): Variable_elision.md now states that a placeholder occurs only in its own local's slot, since pushed locals are aliased rather than elided; the every-slot loop in createElidedVariables could be narrowed to the local slots, and its 'wonky' comment rewritten to say so.  Still moot once avail-zv7 removes placeholders.
close_reason: Moot: VariablePlaceholderDescriptor and the every-slot replacement in createElidedVariables are removed; freezing writes only the frozen slots

title: Experiment: let a postponed creation pass a clearing get
description: Experiment: when a postponed L2_CREATE_VARIABLE (or a postponed Set) reaches an L2_GET_AND_CLEAR_IF_MUTABLE_UNESCAPED_LOCAL_VARIABLE, replace the get with a move of the known value plus a jump to the success (or failure, if known nil) edge, and keep the creation postponed with nil as its initial value, since the clearing read leaves the variable empty.  Determine what the current override in L2_GET_AND_CLEAR_IF_MUTABLE_UNESCAPED_LOCAL_VARIABLE.regenerateForPostponement already does, whether this rewrite is sound when the variable is immutable (clearing is skipped then, but an elided variable is never immutable), and whether it measurably reduces boxing or variable creation in L2 listings.  If adopted, describe it in avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Variable_elision.md.
close_reason: Moot: L1 emits a clearing get only for a local's last read, and L2 preserves that, so the postponed Create x := y stays postponed until an escape; the immutability pass makes y immutable before the move if the Create is emitted downstream.

title: Remove L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS
description:
Remove L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS and everything that existed to feed it: emitCheckLocals and its call sites (after calls, emitSetVariableOffRamp, L1_doSetLiteral), the per-call versioning of elided locals' slots, the TestEscapes/NoEscapes split of CallSiteHelper's junctions and useAnswer's flag, mightMakeEscapedVariableShared on instructions and primitives, and Primitive.Flag.MightMakeEscapedVariableShared.

Why it is safe: since aliased locals are never elided (b7aadbfb1), an elided local's variable object is held only by its own frame, so nothing else can share it or give it a reactor.  Its frame's continuation becomes reachable only by being made immutable or shared, and that runs createElidedVariables, which switches the continuation to DefaultL1Chunk, so the L2 code never resumes with a shared or reactive elided local.
notes:
Since b7aadbfb1 (avail-9dm): Check lists only elided locals; aliased locals (variable pushed anywhere) use the general variable instructions and are never checked.  avail-zv7 (uniform variables) would remove L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS altogether, which may make this moot.
Evidence (2026-11-17): with OptimizationLevel countdowns forced to 10, a probe in A_Variable.staticCheckForSharedOrReactors recorded 33,365 executions of the check across the full test suite, none of which found a shared or reactive local; all tests passed.  Mark ruled the whole mechanism removed, including the primitive flag, since the distinctions are not expected to return (git history holds them).
close_reason: Removed L2_CHECK_ESCAPED_LOCALS and its supporting code; it could never fire once aliased locals stopped being elided (33,365 forced-optimization executions, none fired).

title: Update copyright years to 2026 in Kotlin, Avail, and Java sources
description:
Bring every Avail Foundation copyright notice up to the current year:
"Copyright © 1993-2026, The Avail Foundation, LLC."  This covers the Kotlin
sources (.kt, and the .kts build scripts that carry the header), the Avail
